News.title: What is ‘No10 North’ and where will it be? Andy Burnham’s plan explained
News.content:
ANDY Burnham is set to rewrite the rulebook of British politics by bringing Downing Street to the North.

The new Prime Minister has promised to launch “No10 North”, a new hub designed to take decision-making out of Westminster and hand it back to local communities.

But what actually is this new Northern powerhouse, where is it going, and will it make a real difference to your everyday life?



Where will No10 North be?

The long-term plan is to house No10 North at the brand-new Manchester Digital Campus.



This cutting-edge civil service hub is currently being built on a former brownfield site (previously a Toys ‘R’ Us retail park) off Great Ancoats Street, New Islington.

The existing No10 at Downing Street was first used as a Prime Minister’s residence 300 years ago.

The new, northern version will be a cutting-edge, state-of-the-art office building – think glass walls, open-plan workspaces, and high-tech digital infrastructure.



Because the Prime Minister and high-ranking cabinet officials will be working there, the site will require heavy government-grade security.

The campus will have purpose-built, secure perimeters, restricted access, and specialised communications systems to handle top-secret intelligence, ensuring Burnham and his staff can work safely.

While the permanent campus is not expected to be fully completed until 2028, it will eventually home up to 8,800 civil servants.

But Burnham wants No10 North up and running from day one of his premiership.



Because the Ancoats site isn’t yet ready, his team is currently hunting for an interim city-centre base to be announced “in due course”.

Rumours are already swirling that the temporary office could be set up in Heron House, which already houses GCHQ’s Manchester outpost.

How will it work?

Burnham has made it clear he has no intention of fully packing his bags for London.

He plans to continue living in Greater Manchester, and will spend at least one day a week working directly from No10 North.

The rest of his week will be split between London and regional visits.



When Burnham is down south holding the fort in Whitehall, the Northern headquarters won’t just sit empty.

It’ll be run day-to-day by a team expected to be lead by Caroline Simpson, the current Chief Executive of the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA).

She will oversee a new Devolution Department, also based in Manchester, to ensure regional policies are driven by people who actually live there.

What will No10 North mean for the North?

For decades, Northern voters have felt ignored by a London-centric Westminster bubble.

Burnham says No10 North will be the “nerve centre of a rewired Britain,” aiming to fix this divide.



He insists it’s about real power, not just a fancy new logo, and has set out three key priorities for the Manchester hub:

Public Ownership: Pushing to bring essential utilities like water, energy, and housing back into public hands.

Pushing to bring essential utilities like water, energy, and housing back into public hands. Re-industrialisation: Rebuilding the North’s manufacturing and green-energy sectors.

Rebuilding the North’s manufacturing and green-energy sectors. Regeneration: Pouring investment into left-behind towns and fixing broken transport links.

He said: “Our plans will move decision-making out of Whitehall and into cities like Manchester, to ensure national policy is informed by local expertise.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But critics argue that having two competing No10s will lead to turf wars between London and Manchester.

Others worry that other Northern regions – like Yorkshire or the North East – might feel left out of a “Manchester-centric” government.

News.title: Inside reclusive Ann Widdecombe murder suspect’s council house with news clippings of Farage pinned to the walls
News.content:
ANN Widdecombe’s reclusive murder suspect pinned newspaper clippings about Nigel Farage and Reform UK to the walls in his council house.

Sources said police discovered a mass of articles at Joshua Kerry’s address during his arrest.



The discovery and a forensic search of his devices led terror cops to take full charge of the investigation amid a growing belief that the 78-year-old former MP’s death was politically motivated.

One source said: “The articles on the walls were all about Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, his party and their immigration policies.

“Other discoveries saw Counter Terrorism officers take overall charge of the police investigation.



“It would appear he had a profound dislike of the party, its leader and its policies.”

Police believe Strictly star and Reform immigration spokeswoman Ann was battered to death at her Devon home on July 8 at around 12.30pm.

CCTV footage obtained by The Sun showed Kerry leaving his home in Rotherham, South Yorks, just before 8am that day.

An object described by neighbours as “a wooden baton” was sticking out of the pocket of his shorts.

The footage also showed him pulling back on to his driveway at around 6pm.



Police believe he had completed a 540-mile round trip to and from her home on Dartmoor.

Her body was found at around 11.40am the next day.

A Ring doorbell camera at her home provided police with the crucial breakthrough.



Kerry was last night still being quizzed at a central London police station.

News.title: Woman found dead after altercation outside house in UK city as man, 66, charged with murder
News.content:
'MURDER' PROBE Woman found dead after altercation outside house in UK city as man, 66, charged with murder

A WOMAN has been found dead outside a home, as a 66-year-old man has been charged with murder.

Cops, including specially trained firearms officers, attended a report of an altercation outside a property on St Vincent Road, Newport, in the early hours of Saturday, Gwent Police said.

A woman was pronounced dead by paramedics a short distance away near Chepstow Road, according to the force.

Paramedics battled to save her life but she tragically could not be saved.





On Sunday, police said Albert Williams, from Newport, had been charged with murder following the incident and remanded into custody.

Detective Superintendent Matt Sedgebeer said: “Our enquiries are ongoing, we continue to have a significant police presence in the area, and I ask anyone with any information that can help the investigation to contact us.

“One man has now been charged with murder and with this in mind, I’d ask people not to speculate about this case online while the legal process takes its course

“Such comments can have an impact on our ability to bring anyone, found to have committed a criminal offence, to justice.”

Anyone with information, including CCTV or dashcam footage between the hours of 1am and 3am on Saturday, that may help the investigation has been urged to contact police by calling 101 quoting log reference 2600229981 or through the force’s website.

Information can also be provided anonymously via independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111 or online.

The woman’s family has been informed and is being supported by specialist officers.

Williams is due to appear at Newport Magistrates’ Court on Monday, police added.

News.title: US finds ‘unidentified remains’ in search for MIA soldier after two service members killed during Iran strikes
News.content:
THE US army has found “unidentified remains” in the search for a missing soldier, its central command announced.

It comes after two service members were killed in Iranian ballistic missile and drone attacks in Jordan on Friday.



The first two deaths in Jordan were announced by US Central Command (Centcom) yesterday.

Centcom said on Sunday: “After a thorough search, U.S. military personnel found unidentified remains at the location earlier today.



“An examination process to verify the remains is ongoing.”

A third US service member died in northern Iraq, Centcom added.



They were “killed in action July 18 during a controlled detonation of unexploded ordnance from a downed Iranian one-way attack drone”, American military chiefs said.

A second service member was injured in the same incident.

The identities of the dead and missing American military personnel have not been released.

Donald Trump launched huge revenge strikes against Iran last night after the two US service members’ deaths.



The third soldier was missing in action as the first two deaths were announced and at least four others were injured.

Deaths were confirmed shortly after reports emerged of at least two Iranian missiles hitting the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan – a hub that hosts American troops and fighter jets.

Footage from the Jordanian base showed at least two impacts and an blast.



But the US army did not confirm where exactly the two service members were killed.

In retaliation, US Central Command (Centcom) confirmed on Saturday that they had unleashed a fresh blitz on Iran.

They said the attacks would “swiftly punish” the regime for taking American lives.

The deaths bring the American toll of the war to 16 – but the two service members confirmed dead on Friday were the first to be killed by direct fire from Iran since it broke out.

And it’s the first time US troops have been killed since the ceasefire collapsed two weeks ago, with Trump declaring it “over” after several exchanges of fire.



The US and Iran have ramped up attacks in the weeks since – last night’s revenge strikes on the rogue nation marked the eighth night in the row that Trump has blitzed Iran.

In last night’s huge barrage of attacks, Centcom said the US has hit Iranian coastal surveillance and air defence facilities, Iranian forces and weapon storage sites.

Speaking to NY Post on Saturday, the US president said the soldiers had died “in service to their country”.

He added: “And it’s a shame, but in this case, they died because they don’t want to see Iran have a nuclear weapon and they don’t want to see the Middle East blown up”.

The US also blitzed several bridges in southern Iran this week, as well as ports and surveillance towers.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Iranian authorities said a nuclear plant that was hit as it was still being built, leading the UN’s nuclear watchdog to call for restraint.

News.title: Person rushed to hospital as dockside crane collapses onto ship at major port
News.content:
CRANE CRASH Person rushed to hospital as dockside crane collapses onto ship at major port

ONE PERSON has been rushed to hospital after a crane collapsed onto a ship at a major port.

The emergency services raced to the Port of Tyne in South Shields, Tyne and Wear at around 1.02pm today.



The incident involved a dockside crane.

Crews from North East Ambulance Service and the Great North Air Ambulance were dispatched to respond to the incident after one person was injured.



A spokesperson for North East Ambulance Service said: “We were called to an incident in which a person was injured at the Port of Tyne, South Shields, at 1.02pm on 19 July.

“We dispatched three double crewed ambulances, two clinical team leaders, a duty officer, three vehicles from our Hazardous Area Response Team (HART) and were supported by Great North Air Ambulance Service. One patient was taken to the Royal Victoria Infirmary.



“One of our HART vehicles remains at the scene on standby to support the fire service.”

Northumbria Police said the man’s condition was not thought to be life threatening.



A police spokesperson said: “Just after 13:00 today, we received a report of concern for the safety of a person at the Port of Tyne in South Shields.

“It was reported that, for reasons yet to be established, a ship had collided with a crane.

“Emergency services attended and a man was found to have sustained injuries not believed to be life-threatening.”

The man remains in hospital and enquiries are ongoing.

Photos of the devastation appear to show damage to a crane and several containers on a BG Freight Line vessel.



Mike, who handles the YouTube channel Urbex Drone View, saw the aftermath and saw the emergency services arriving as he was approaching form the north of the River Tyne.

He told ChronicleLIve: “When I arrived on the north side to get some drone footage, I was met with the tangled wreckage of the dockside crane, highlighting the sheer force of the incident.

“Behind a line of emergency service vehicles, I could also see that several cargo containers aboard the BG Orange had been dislodged from their original positions, as shown in the accompanying photographs.”

He added: “It was quite horrific to see something like that.

“You don’t know who’s injured. I think certainly a major incident was declared.



“The amount of emergency vehicles there: fire engines, ambulances, and from what I’ve heard two air ambulances were deployed.”

Mike told the news outlet: “Seeing the extent of the damage brought home just how serious the incident was.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It is difficult to imagine what those working on the dock or aboard the vessel must have experienced at that moment.

“My thoughts are with everyone involved and their families, and I sincerely hope that all those affected are safe and receive the support they need.”

News.title: Tourist killed in hit-and-run near historic Spanish town with cops finding his dismembered arm & leg
News.content:
GRUESOME DISCOVERY Tourist killed in hit-and-run near historic Spanish town with cops finding his dismembered arm & leg

A TOURIST has been killed in a gruesome hit-and-run on a Spanish holiday island.

Cops found a dismembered arm and leg after the horror crash near the historic town of Capdepera, Majorca.



The tourist was on holiday with his wife and young son when the tragedy unfolded.

Police think the 55-year-old Swiss man had gone out for a run when he was struck by a car.



The crash appears to have sent the pedestrian flying.

The driver, a 21-year-old Spanish man, did not stop after hitting the man at around 7am on Sunday. cops said.



He is thought to have been on his way to work at a local hotel.

The man continued driving to work, before calling his cousin for help and returning to the scene of the crash on the Cala Mesquida road.

As the man arrived at the scene with his relative, they found a watch, an arm and a leg within minutes, and called the police.

Cops rushed to the scene, but it took them two hours of intense searching to find the rest of the tourist’s body.



It was found trapped in bushes far from the road, and firefighters had to be called to free it from the undergrowth.

The driver had an anxiety attack at the scene and received treatment.

He tested positive for alcohol, police said, and officers arrested him at the side of the road.

The man is under investigation for manslaughter, failure to render aid, and driving under the influence of alcohol, police said.

Investigators said he may have been driving his Volkswagen Polo at high speed, as the body was found more than 330ft from where the arm was discovered.



It comes seven people including two children were injured when a car ploughed into a busy terrace bar on the Costa del Sol.

Terrifying footage showed a 47-year-old woman driving a white Peugeot through the streets of Frigiliana in the seconds before disaster.

In just a few terrifying seconds the driver careened through a crowd of diners, also taking out the restaurant’s tables and umbrellas.

Seven people were left injured, including two children aged five and 14.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The adult victims included three women aged 48, 79, and 45, and two men aged 44 and 77.



Six of the victims were taken to the nearby La Axarquia Hospital, while the seventh received medical attention at a health care centre in Nerja.

News.title: Doctor, 68, and wife, 62, die in horror plane crash as pilot rushed to hospital in Brazil
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

AIRCRAFT TRAGEDY Doctor, 68, and wife, 62, die in horror plane crash as pilot rushed to hospital in Brazil

A PIONEERING doctor and his wife have been killed in a horror plane crash.

The couple were flying shortly after the doctor had attended his dad’s funeral.



Doctor Ederson da Silva, 68, and his wife Roseli Amarilda Pechulo Silva, 62, died after their small plane plummeted to the ground in Palmas, northern Brazil.

Witnesses said the aircraft crashed to the ground shortly after take off.



They said the plane appeared to take off normally before suddenly dropping out of the sky.

A large crack was heard, police said.



Emergency services rushed to the scene of the crash.

Roseli was found dead – but Doctor Ederson was pulled alive from the wreckage.

He was treated by paramedics but they were unable save him and he died at the scene.

Their pilot survived the crash and was rushed to hospital with serious injuries.



He was identified as Hamilton Lopes da Conceição by police.

He remains in Palmas General Hospital, where his condition was described as unstable by cops.

The couple owned the São Lucas Hospital and lived together in Redenção.



Shocking photos showed the twisted wreck of the plane as it crashed into a farm.

An investigation has been launched into the air tragedy.

In May, an elderly pilot was found alive more than 24 hours after a plane crash.

Altevir Edson, 72, was feared dead after his small plane fell out of the sky over a dense forest near Belém, northern Brazil.

Altevir’s single-engine aircraft got into difficulty when a vulture flew into its propeller.



When the wreck of the plane was discovered, Altevir was nowhere to be seen.

The 72-year-old is thought to have wandered into the dense vegetation to look for help after the crash.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But he quickly became disorientated and lost.

The pilot was eventually found more than three miles from the crash site, after search and rescue teams deployed sniffer dogs and a drone to look for him.

News.title: Woman, 49, charged after pensioner ‘murdered’ at block of flats
News.content:
'MURDER' PROBE Woman, 49, charged after pensioner ‘murdered’ at block of flats

A WOMAN has been charged with murder after a pensioner was found dead in a block of flats.

The 75-year-old man died at Hargreaves House on Crook Street near Ormrod Street, Bolton, at around 8am on July 17.



Police have charged Samantha Nuttall, 49, from Bolton, with murder and she has been remanded into custody ahead of an appearance at Manchester and Salford Magistrates’ Court on Monday.

Greater Manchester Police said the victim had been formally identified and his next of kin had been informed.



Det Insp Louise Kelly has appealed for information and said: “I would like to express my deepest condolences to the victim’s family and loved ones as they navigate through this loss.

“They will continue to be supported by our specialist officers during this difficult time.”

News.title: Big Issue founder urges Andy Burnham to give councils stronger powers to buy-up empty homes
News.content:
Big Issue founder urges Andy Burnham to give councils stronger powers to buy-up empty homes

EXCLUSIVE: The call from Big Issue founder Lord John Bird comes as more than one million families languish on waiting lists and record levels of children are forced to live in temporary accommodation

View 2 Images There are an estimated 300,000 homes in England that have been left empty for more than six months (Image: Getty Images)

Andy Burnham has been urged to give councils stronger powers to buy-up or lease empty properties and help tackle the homelessness crisis.

‌



The call from Big Issue founder Lord John Bird comes as more than one million families languish on waiting lists and record levels of children are forced to live in temporary accommodation, including B&Bs.

‌



The crossbench peer is calling for a government-backed loan scheme, which he said would “unlock thousands of new social houses and ease the homelessness crisis”.

‌



He told The Mirror: “Andy Burnham has an opportunity to show he’s serious about tackling homelessness by introducing this on day one of his premiership.”

Lord Bird said: “Across the country, properties sit empty while families languish on waiting lists and councils break the bank to put them in temporary accommodation.

View 2 Images Big Issue founder Lord John Bird has demanded action from Andy Burnham on housing crisis (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

‌



“This incoming government must think differently if it wants to find long-term solutions to the problems we face.

“A government-backed loan scheme for councils to lease or buy up empty homes is an obvious way to unlock thousands of new social houses and ease the homelessness crisis.”

The crossbench peer has tabled amendments to the Social Housing Bill in the Lords this week in an attempt to bring thousands of empty homes back into use for social housing.

‌



It aims to reduce the qualifying period for Empty Dwelling Management Orders (EDMOs) from two years to six months, allowing councils to intervene early.

There are an estimated 300,000 homes in England that have been left empty for more than six months. Meanwhile, more than 1.3million households are stuck on social housing waiting lists, according to the charity Shelter.

Andy Burnham's 10 major challenges and headaches as he enters No10 as PM READ MORE :

Lord Bird’s amendment would also establish a government-backed loan scheme to help councils purchase or lease the empty properties - before renovating them.

Article continues below

Incoming Prime Minister Mr Burnham has previously made clear that the housing crisis will be a priority for the government. During a major speech earlier this month he pledged the “biggest council housebuilding programme since the postwar period” in office.

He said the country was stuck in a "housing trap" with nearly 1.5 million fewer council homes since the 1980s when Margaret Thatcher's Right to Buy policy triggered a massive drop in public housing stock.

News.title: 'Andy Burnham must turn his hope into policies that actually change lives'
News.content:
'Andy Burnham must turn his hope into policies that actually change lives'

Andy Burnham, the new Labour leader, will set out his domestic priorities in his first speech from Downing Street on Monday after formally taking over from Sir Keir Starmer

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

Andy Burnham enters Downing Street on Monday promising a bolder, more ambitious government.

‌



Millions will welcome the change in tone. Britain needs urgency, honesty and a Prime Minister willing to confront failures that have been allowed to continue for too long.

‌



His reported readiness to tackle the broken water industry would be a strong place to start. Privatisation has delivered sewage, debt and huge rewards for bosses while customers pay the price.

‌



The plan for a Number 10 North also deserves a fair hearing. Power has been hoarded in Westminster for decades, leaving towns and cities feeling ignored. Governing from beyond London could help change that, provided it brings real decisions, jobs and investment rather than another sign on a door.

Mr Burnham will speak of hope on Monday. The country has heard plenty of speeches before. His task is to turn that hope into lower bills, better public services and a fairer deal for working families.

Article continues below

Back the BBC

For £180 a year, the BBC still gives Britain something no streaming giant can match. It informs, educates and entertains across television, radio and online, while supporting thousands of jobs and adding billions to the economy.

Romesh Ranganathan's playful remake of the classic John Cleese film is a timely reminder of that value as ministers debate the Corporation's future. The BBC is not perfect. It must keep earning trust, spend money wisely and serve audiences who now have more choice than ever.

But losing it would leave Britain poorer, less informed and less connected. From trusted news and children's learning to sport, drama, music and moments that bring the nation together, the BBC remains part of the country's fabric. That is surely worth protecting.

News.title: Spain's hottest week of summer as 45C scorcher hits Brit tourist spots next week
News.content:
Spain's hottest week of summer as 45C scorcher hits Brit tourist spots next week

The high temperatures will affect southeastern Spain, Guadalquivir valley, Ebro valley, northeastern depressions, Pyrenees valleys and inland Mallorca

View 3 Images People cooling off on a beach in Valencia during a previous heatwave at the beginning of July (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Spain will battle temperatures exceeding 45C as parts of the Iberian peninsula are set to go through yet another heatwave.

‌



Aemet, Spain's equivalent of the Met Office, announced the heatwave will come into force on Tuesday, July 21, and will remain in place until at least Thursday, July 23. Previously, Hugo Morán, Aemet's president and Spain's secretary of state for the environment, told local media that the country has entered a chain of successive heatwaves.

‌



The latest heatwave will affect southeastern Spain, Guadalquivir valley, Ebro valley, northeastern depressions, Pyrenees valleys and inland Mallorca. Aemet states: "The blocking pattern, formed by a stationary cut-off low northwest of the Iberian Peninsula, combined with a mid-level high over North Africa, is causing a mass of warm, dry air laden with suspended dust to intrude over southeastern Spain and the Balearic Islands.

‌



"This air mass will spread across much of the country in the coming days. Combined with the sunshine typical of this time of year and widespread subsidence, temperatures are expected to rise gradually, reaching very high values next week."

The agency explained that there is a "significant or even extraordinary" risk to those taking part in outdoor activities and those vulnerable, including the elderly or those with cardiovascular diseases. While Aemet couldn't state for certain when the heatwave will end due to various factors, it said that temperatures are likely to "continue at dangerous levels until next weekend".

On Monday, temperatures are expected to be high in the eastern and southeastern thirds of the peninsula, as well as in the Balearic Islands. They will reach 36-38C, with some places going up to 40C.

‌



Up to 42C are then possible on Tuesday in low-lying areas and inland Mallorca, with temperatures of up to 39C in the other areas affected by the heatwave. The peak of the heatwave will then hit between Wednesday and Thursday, Aemet said.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Temperatures will continue to rise along the Mediterranean coast on Thursday due to westerly winds, reaching up to 44C. Aemet said: "On Friday the 24th, uncertainty increases considerably.

‌



"Although the most likely scenario at the moment is the arrival of a cooler air mass from the northwest of the Iberian Peninsula, which would initiate a temperature drop that would become more widespread in the following days, it cannot be ruled out that this arrival could be delayed for a few more days, prolonging the heatwave.

"In any case, it is likely that on Friday temperatures will remain high in many areas." Nights will also remain very warm, with popular tourist areas like Malaga, Alicante and Barcelona being at medium or high health risk due to the extreme heat.

People have been urged by Spain's ministry of health to drink water regularly, stay cool and avoid direct sun exposure during the middle of the day, when temperatures will peak. Those most at risk are the elderly, pregnant women, children under four years old, people with chronic illnesses and people who work outdoors.

‌



View 3 Images A map of health risk levels for Sunday, July 19 (Image: Ministerio de Sanidad)

This will be Spain's third heatwave so far this summer. Wildfire danger levels will also continue to increase as a result of the extreme temperatures, as major blazes are already raging in Zaragoza and Guadalajara.

‌



Euronews reports that the two forest fires have been burning out of control for several days. The most serious of the two is the one near Orés, Zaragoza, which has been evaluated as the worst one this year, burning an area of around 15,400 hectares, with a perimetre of about 60km.

The second fire, in Sierra Norte de Guadalajara in La Mierla, has been burning since the middle of this week. The blaze has already affected around 6,000 hectares, with local authorities not optimistic about its evolution.

View 3 Images Fire hazard levels appear to peak on Friday according to Aemet (Image: Aemet)

Article continues below

This year's average temperature has beat the previous record set in 2024 by 0.4C. Between June 1 and July 15, the average temperature in Spain was 3.3C above the normal values for this time of the year.

News.title: 'Andy Burnham tackling cost of living is the way to stop UK doom-scrolling through PMs'
News.content:
Theresa May pledged to tackle the nation’s “burning injustices”.

Boris Johnson promised to level up the country.

Liz Truss told a weary public they could “ride out the storm”.

Rishi Sunak vowed to fix the mistakes of Liz Truss.

‌



Keir Starmer set out his mission of “national renewal”.

All were visions - with varying degrees of success - set out in their first address to the country as Prime Minister in front of Downing Street’s famous black door.

In less than 24 hours, it will be the turn of Andy Burnham - the so-called King of the North, who sensationally returned to Parliament last month.

After being invited to form a government by the King, the new Labour leader will deliver one of the most important speeches of his political career.

‌



Andy Burnham's 10 major challenges and headaches as he enters No10 as PM READ MORE :

It will be his chance to introduce himself to the country as Prime Minister and set the tone of his government for years to come. The stakes couldn't be higher.

With the world’s media gathered on make-shift platforms - erected by scaffolders in recent days - Burnham will acknowledge a nation weary at the frequent sight of the No10 podium.

He will insist he is “acutely conscious” of the doom-scrolling of Prime Ministers as the sixth to walk up the street in the space of a decade.

But crucially, it will be his promise to give Britain “more breathing space” on the cost of living that will prick up ears in homes across the country. The burden on cash-strapped families is at the top of voters’ concerns — and it has been the case for some time.

‌



Polling by YouGov earlier this year found that no political party has a firm lead on who is best to handle the issue at the forefront of the public’s mind.

And in March just 10% said Starmer’s government was handling the issue well.

If Burnham’s team want to end merry-go-round of Prime Ministers, tackling the pain of the cost of living crisis head on is the right place to start.

It would be understandable if hard-pressed households - forced to endure years of hikes in energy, water, food, and council tax bills - are jaded by politicians’ promises.

‌



It is why Burnham’s delivery in the coming days, months, and years is critical.

Monday's speech will be a major moment in the country's history, but easing the pain on households will be key if this new government is to succeed.

News.title: UK weather maps show exact date the mercury could plummet -11C below July average
News.content:
UK weather maps show exact date the mercury could plummet -11C below July average

The UK is forecast to see a dramatic weather change after weeks of scorching conditions, with WXCharts predicting temperatures could fall as much as 11C below the July average

View 3 Images Weather map showing cooler temperatures on July 28 (Image: WXCharts)

UK temperatures are set to plummet after weeks of sweltering heat, according to the latest forecasts.

‌



WXCharts has forecast a significant drop in temperatures on July 28, with some areas seeing mercury levels fall as low as 6C. The south of England and East Anglia will be the warmest, with highs of 14C and 15C expected in Norwich, London, Canterbury, Oxford, Bristol, Portsmouth, and Exeter.

‌



The Midlands and parts of the north, including Birmingham, Nottingham, and Manchester, will see temperatures ranging between 12C and 13C. Wales, including Cardiff and Conwy, and Northern Ireland, including Belfast and Derry, will experience highs of 10C to 12C.

‌



But it will be far colder across the north of England and south of Scotland. The mercury is expected fall to single figures in the likes of Newcastle, Carlisle, Edinburgh, and Dumfries in the coming days.

News.title: Port Tyne crane incident: Huge 999 response as person taken to hospital and scene described as 'horrific'
News.content:
Port Tyne crane incident: Huge 999 response as person taken to hospital and scene described as 'horrific'

Crews from North East Ambulance Service and the Great North Air Ambulance were sent to the scene in South Shields, Tyne and Wear

View 3 Images BG freight line ship on the port of Tyne with a collapsed crane (Image: Newcastle Chronicle)

One person has been taken to hospital after a crane collapse at a port in England.

‌



Crews from various emergency services were sent to the scene of the incident at the Port of Tyne in South Shields, Tyne and Wear. The incident involved a dockside crane and took place this afternoon, at around 1.02pm.

‌



Crews from North East Ambulance Service and the Great North Air Ambulance were sent to respond to the incident after one person was injured. A spokesperson for North East Ambulance Service said: "We were called to an incident in which a person was injured at the Port of Tyne, South Shields, at 1.02pm on 19 July.

‌



"We dispatched three double crewed ambulances, two clinical team leaders, a duty officer, three vehicles from our Hazardous Area Response Team (HART) and were supported by Great North Air Ambulance Service. One patient was taken to the Royal Victoria Infirmary.

"One of our HART vehicles remains at the scene on standby to support the fire service." Photos from the scene show damage to a crane and several containers on a BG Freight Line vessel.

View 3 Images A picture of the damaged crane (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

‌



Mike, who runs YouTube channel Urbex Drone View, heard about the incident online and saw the aftermath, ChronicleLive reports. He saw the emergency services at the scene when he was approaching from the north of the River Tyne.

Mike said: "When I arrived on the north side to get some drone footage, I was met with the tangled wreckage of the dockside crane, highlighting the sheer force of the incident. Behind a line of emergency service vehicles, I could also see that several cargo containers aboard the BG Orange had been dislodged from their original positions, as shown in the accompanying photographs."

Mike added: "It was quite horrific to see something like that. You don’t know who’s injured. I think certainly a major incident was declared. The amount of emergency vehicles there: fire engines, ambulances, and from what I've heard two air ambulances were deployed."

Article continues below

View 3 Images A dockside crane lies on the container ship BG Orange operated by BG Freight Line (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

The drone operator continued: "Seeing the extent of the damage brought home just how serious the incident was. It is difficult to imagine what those working on the dock or aboard the vessel must have experienced at that moment.

"My thoughts are with everyone involved and their families, and I sincerely hope that all those affected are safe and receive the support they need."

News.title: Burnham to promise 'more breathing room' for people in first speech as PM
News.content:
Andy Burnham will promise to give people "more breathing room" when he gives his first speech as prime minister outside No 10 on Monday.

He is expected to say he is "acutely conscious" of the UK's high turnover of prime ministers - and that politics needs to be more stable and responsible.

And he is expected to characterise the moment as one of "reflection and resolution", arguing Britain must be honest about the challenges it faces.

Burnham will officially replace Sir Keir Starmer and become the UK's 59th prime minister - and seventh in 10 years - on Monday, following a meeting with King Charles III.

Earlier, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the incoming prime minister was a "people pleaser" at a time when the country needed someone who could "take tough decisions, who can face down Labour MPs".

"The job is not a popularity contest. It is making the lives of all of the people outside this building better. And he has not said what he's going to do. It's all airy-fairy stuff," she said.

Burnham was officially declared Labour Party leader on Friday following a short contest in which he was the only candidate, having secured the backing of 379 MPs.

Some opposition parties have urged Burnham to call a general election in order to ensure he has a mandate for his premiership.

However, earlier Labour's deputy leader Lucy Powell insisted Burnham would stick to the promises made in Labour's manifesto in the 2024 general election but will be more ambitious.

"He really understands the bigger, bolder measures that are needed to live up to the manifesto promises," she told the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg programme.

News.title: Thames Water lenders preparing legal challenge in event of Burnham nationalisation
News.content:
The lenders to Thames Water are preparing a legal challenge in case a Burnham-led government attempts to nationalise the UK's biggest water company.

Burnham - who takes over as PM on Monday - has previously said he wants to see "greater public control" of the water and energy sectors and has called for Thames Water to be nationalised.

Thames Water is about Â£20bn in debt.

Its lenders had proposed a deal to write off nearly half of that and inject new cash in return for some leniency from future pollution fines, but this deal has previously been rejected by the government as being "weak" and bad for consumers and the environment.

Sources close to the creditors have told the BBC that in the event of full nationalisation, they would pursue payment in full of the outstanding debts as has happened in previous cases, which could leave the government with a multi-billion-pound bill.

Fears first emerged three years ago that Thames Water could collapse and on Thursday, the firm warned it has enough cash to last until the end of this year.

Creditors insisted on Sunday that they were still working with officials and regulators to reach an agreement to rescue the company.

A spokesperson for the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs said the government was "prepared for any eventuality".

"Thames Water customers have been let down for far too long, with 15 years of under-performance, increasing serious pollution, and customers left to pick up the bill," the spokesperson said.

"The secretary of state has written to Ofwat to outline her early views that she is not convinced Londonâ¯andâ¯Valleyâ¯Water's proposal is good enough for consumers or the environment."

The lenders have offered to write off Â£9.4bn of Thames Water's near Â£20bn debt pile and put Â£3.35bn of cash into the company, but in return they want leniency from future pollution fines in order to turn the firm's fortune's around.

Objecting to the proposal, Emma Reynolds said in June that she did not want a scenario where Thames Water customers had to "pick up the bill for the company's failures".

At the time, she told reporters that the government "stands ready for all eventualities", including temporary nationalisation.

When asked in a Sky News interview on Sunday whether a Burnham government would nationalise Thames Water, Labour's deputy leader Lucy Powell said: "Let's see".

"This has been an ongoing issue and concern in government," she said.

"The government has powers to to bring a distressed water company under special measures, and let's see if the government needs to, wants to use those powers."

Powell added that "the privatisation of water hasn't worked".

"It's not created competition. What you've seen is bills going up and up and up over years and years and years. Investment not being being made ... and then now these companies are in are in real distress," she said.

There is a halfway house, in which Thames would be placed into a so called "special administration regime", or SAR, which is usually a temporary situation until another private sector buyer can be found.

The existing lenders have made it clear that they would be prepared to join the bidders for Thames in that scenario.

However, comments from the incoming prime minister Andy Burnham that key utilities should be under increased "public control" make it hard to imagine that the government will have much political appetite to find a new set of private sector owners for a company that serves 16 million people which means that a temporary nationalisation might become permanent.

But under either a SAR or full nationalisation, Thames ongoing problems could then leave taxpayers footing the bill for Thames cash shortfalls - a figure that Thames Water management puts at Â£2bn by the end of next year.

Whatever happens, its customers' taps and loos will still function, but the future of Thames Water is a key policy test for the new administration.

News.title: Record numbers of honours for working class heroes
News.content:
"I always had the perception that you only got an honour if you were rich or famous," says Clive Lawrence.

His start in life had been free school meals and growing up on a council estate in Derbyshire, but the former head teacher has been made an Officer of the British Empire (OBE).

He's part of a quiet revolution in the honours system, which has deliberately sought to make the awards less socially exclusive and to have a fairer spread of winners around the country.

That change followed an analysis by the BBC last year of the New Year Honours in 2025 which showed that among higher winners - such as Commanders of the British Empire (CBE), knighthoods and damehoods - only 4% of recipients had grown up in working class backgrounds.

Cabinet Office figures for the New Year Honours 2026 show that for higher awards that has now risen to 31%, a record level.

News.title: Chinese firm seeks compensation over British Steel nationalisation
News.content:
The former owner of British Steel has said it will pursue the British government for compensation after the loss-making firm was nationalised.

The UK took control of the Scunthorpe steelworks a year ago after China's Jingye Group said it planned to close the site because it was not financially viable, and fully nationalised the plant on Thursday.

In a statement on Sunday, Jingye said it will seek "full compensation through legal means to the very end" over the UK's move.

A government spokesperson said draft compensation regulations due to be released in the autumn will set out a compensation process through which an independent assessor "would determine what, if any, is payable".

Jingye bought the Lincolnshire steel plant in 2020, but in March last year the firm launched a consultation on its closure saying the plant was losing Â£700,000 a day.

The government took control of British Steel operations in April 2025, but until this week it remained under Jingye's ownership which limited the government's ability to shape the firm's future.

On Thursday the UK government said it was taking the firm into public hands in order to safeguard a "vital national capability", giving the government the power to decide the plant's future.

The decision to nationalise British Steel has threatened to strain the relationship between London and Beijing just as Andy Burnham prepares to enter Downing Street as prime minister on Monday.

News.title: Bruno Mars has an unexpected opening before Wembley party starts
News.content:
Bruno Mars appeared determined to lift the nation's mood during the first of his six nights at Wembley Stadium.

His last UK performance came in July 2018, shortly after England had been knocked out of the men's World Cup semi-finals. Eight years later, history had repeated itself.

But wearing an England football scarf, Union Jack bucket hat and clutching a Paddington Bear, the showman energised a 75,000-strong, multi-generational crowd.

After nearly a decade away from UK audiences, Mars proved why fans had snapped up tickets in record numbers, external.

News.title: Fire crews battling blaze on Arthur’s Seat in Edinburgh
News.content:
Fire crews are battling a large blaze on Arthur's Seat in Edinburgh.

A huge plume of white smoke could be seen from as far away as Fife after the fire broke out below Salisbury Crags at about 18:40 on Sunday.

Six appliances were in attendance, with firefighters seen dousing the flames.

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service (SFRS) said there were "no reported casualties" and Police Scotland has closed Queens Drive to all vehicles.

News.title: Madonna, Justin Bieber, Shakira and BTS perform at World Cup half-time show
News.content:
Colombian pop star Shakira and Nigerian musician Burna Boy reunited on stage after performing together at the tournament's opening ceremony in Mexico City last month.

Their collaboration, Dai Dai, has been a global chart hit and has been a fixture in stadiums throughout the tournament.

K-Pop group BTS have been making their comeback from a three-year music hiatus to complete their mandatory military service in South Korea. The band is currently in the midst of an 85-date world tour.

The half-time show has been curated by Coldplay's Chris Martin and will raise money for the Fifa Global Citizen Education Fund, an initiative working to raise $100m (Â£73m) for children worldwide.

News.title: Britain 'set for bumper year' for butterflies
News.content:
A butterfly charity says the UK could be set for a "bumper" year of the insects as it launches its annual appeal for the public to count them.

Butterfly Conservation, based at East Lulworth, in Dorset, said the hot and dry spring meant it was already seeing an increase in several species.

On Friday, it launched its Big Butterfly Count, a yearly event asking members of the public to report the butterflies they see.

Dr Dan Hoare, director of nature recovery at Butterfly Conservation, said it was an opportunity for them to "colonise and reach out to new places".

"I have seen three or four species in the south of England... wandering away from their normal places," he said.

News.title: Digital ID plan to be scrapped in Burnham's first major policy pledge
News.content:
"This reprioritisation of public resource shows a change in direction towards improving everyday life and strengthening local economies over expensive national government schemes."

Plans for a digital ID scheme had initially been introduced by Sir Keir ahead of Labour's conference last year.

At the time, he argued that mandatory digital ID for workers would make it easier to clamp down on immigrants working illegally and modernise the state.

As well as tackling illegal immigration, Sir Keir said a digital ID system would enable citizens to prove identity to access key services quickly instead of having to hunt for utility bills.

The Office for Budget Responsibility estimated last November that the programme would cost Â£1.8bn over three years, but Downing Street rejected this figure.

In January, after nearly three million people signed a parliamentary petition opposing the introduction of digital IDs, the government changed its approach.

Instead, ministers ditched the compulsory part of the scheme and relaunched it as voluntary, saying digital IDs could eventually allow people to do everything from managing their childcare to filling in tax returns on a "one stop" app.

Soon after, Home Affairs Committee Chair Dame Karen Bradley said the government was right to introduce digital ID but had botched the launch.

In a report setting out the committee's investigation into the launch and subsequent changes to the policy, Dame Karen called attempts to set out the plans "nothing short of a fiasco" which "raised fears of government over-reach into people's lives".

Burnham will become prime minister after meeting with King Charles III on Monday, and his office said "one of the first things this government will do is put its focus where people need it right now".

Scrapping digital ID, the spokesperson said, will mean "redirecting the resources earmarked for the scheme towards people's everyday priorities".

Speaking to Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, deputy Labour leader and Burnham ally Lucy Powell said the money saved by scrapping the scheme was "not an insignificant amount" and would be "reprioritised and redistributed in different ways".

"But it's not just about the money - it's actually about the attention and the focus, so that the whole of government machinery can work in service of the agenda and the vision that the Labour government is setting out under Andy Burnham," she said.

News.title: Is Burnham promising a new dawn for North Sea oil and gas?
News.content:
The final weekend before Andy Burnham enters Downing Street is being dominated by suggestions he'll announce plans for new drilling in the North Sea.

On Saturday, the BBC reported the in-coming prime minister would stick to the party's 2024 manifesto pledge to issue no new oil and gas licences but would honour existing ones.

That line has been confirmed as the hours count down to the Burnham premiership.

Speaking on Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Labour's deputy leader Lucy Powell said Burnham would stick to the party's manifesto commitments, but there would be a "change of emphasis" on North Sea oil and gas.

"We've been really clear that the way to achieve in the long term energy security and lower bills is by ensuring that we do have our own homegrown, clean, much cheaper energy," she said.

"But we've been absolutely clear that North Sea gas and oil is an important part of that transition.

"It's an important part of the mix, and I think what Andy's talking about is taking a more pragmatic approach and working with the industry to make sure that it can contribute to that [energy] transition and to the mix that is needed over the long term."

News.title: Parts of UK to get break in heatwave but dry spell to continue
News.content:
Cooler temperatures are on the way for some parts of the UK after a first half of summer dominated by warm, sunny and largely dry weather.

Parts of England have experienced more than two weeks of heatwave conditions, and some central areas have had the longest dry spell since 1997.

But the third heatwave of 2026 is now easing as northerly winds introduce some fresher air - although most places still won't have any significant rainfall.

The slightly cooler spell may be very brief for some parts of southern England and south Wales, where we could see heatwave criteria being reached again later this week.

News.title: Twins share uni, course, grade and graduation day
News.content:
Ainsley said going through university with his brother had made the experience "a lot easier".

"It's kind of like going with a best friend but he's my brother and we can spend even more time together," he said.

Despite being a support for one another, Ainsley said they had a healthy level of competition during their studies.

"We always end up thinking we have to one-up each other. We made these small bets, where if I got a higher grade than him he would have to buy me a McDonalds, for example, it was those little things that made the competitiveness."

Adrian, who is older than Ainsley by a minute, said the competition helped push him academically.

"At the end of the day, we do wish each other the best. Obviously, we always aim to go high in our grades but it's just a bit of a light-hearted thing to push us more.

"I had a couple of exams and assignments where I did lower than Ainsley but that's what pushed me."

Graduating together made it easier for their parents, as they followed one after another in the ceremony.

"It felt surreal. Even from the get-go being able to get ready with my brother for our big day, seeing ourselves together, I felt proud.

"Walking down that aisle hearing my name was great, and knowing my brother was right behind felt great," said Adrian.

For now, the brothers are continuing to stick together as they begin internships â¯in Milton Keynes.

"The only time we'll be separated is in an actual job now," said Ainsley.

News.title: I'll lose my bowel because my pain was dismissed until my husband spoke up
News.content:
An operation nearly 20 years ago left Donna Davies in constant pain but she only felt believed by medics after her husband spoke up.

Donna, 56, now requires her large bowel to be removed because of her vaginal mesh medical device, which was removed after she felt it cutting into her.

It was fitted after Donna, from Swansea, developed stress urinary incontinence in her 30s, and the procedure has since been paused by the NHS.

She was invited to attend a women's health summit in Wales this week, which looked at how women's pain is too often dismissed as "normal" within healthcare.

Donna is one of an estimated 100,000 women in the UK who had the procedure to treat incontinence or prolapse.

She said: "The mesh was leaving me in daily pain - the only way I can explain it was that I was being cut by glass every time I moved.

"I didn't feel as if I was believed and I didn't feel my pain was acknowledged until my husband spoke up about an incident we had and then I felt that the surgeon believed my husband."

The device was eventually removed and a "sling" made from her own muscles was created at the same time as a total hysterectomy.

"I've never recovered from this operation - I'm still in constant pain, neuropathic pain as well and sadly I'm about to lose my large bowel and have a permanent stoma.

"I feel that women in Wales are being forgotten. There are no specialist services in Wales for women like myself, yet nine specialist centres in England - we do feel forgotten."

Delyth Jewell, the women's health minister in the Senedd, said she wanted rules to be strengthened so that health boards are required to include women in the design of services for them.

"I am determined to strengthen women's voices so that women will be believed about their bodies," the minister said at the women's health summit.

"I wonder how many women will have heard the words 'this might hurt' when they go to the doctor?

"That shouldn't be normal. Too often women's health services are considered a 'should' not a 'must'.

"We need to make sure that in theatre space they are prioritised more, we need to be making sure that training is improved."

News.title: Eight released over alleged threat to Islamic event
News.content:
Eight more people have been freed from custody, as police continue to investigate an alleged extreme right-wing threat to an Islamic event in Suffolk.

Officers became aware of the threat to the UK Ijtima event at Shrubland Hall, near Ipswich, last weekend.

Thousands of people attended the gathering but it closed early on police advice.

The Metropolitan Police said on Saturday, external that seven men were released from custody without charge, while another man was released on bail with strict conditions pending further inquiries.

The force said the investigation involved searching homes and vehicles, and more than 35 digital devices were seized.

Following those searches, a 42-year-old man was charged with two counts of possession of offensive weapons, extendable batons, and possession of a stun gun.

Police said the charges were not believed to be connected to the alleged threat on UK Ijtima.

The man was remanded in custody to appear at Reading Magistrates' Court on Monday.

Four other people were previously released on bail pending further inquiries.

News.title: Woman killed while asleep with baby ‘was my world’, sister says
News.content:
The sister of a 24-year-old mother who was stabbed and killed as she lay in bed with her husband and baby in west London has said "she was my world".

Kirandeep Kaur, who was originally from India, was fatally attacked at her home in Hayes on 12 July.

Speaking through a translator from the Majha region of Punjab, India, her sister Gursharan told BBC London: "She is everything for me, she video calls me and my mum. What are we going to do without her?"

A man has been charged with Kaur's murder.

Gursharan, who is 21, said her sister came to London looking for a better job so she could support her family.

"My sister moved to the UK in September 2024 to study at Buckinghamshire New University.

"She completed her studies and worked at a grocery store.

"We spoke to each other on the phone. But she hasn't been back, so I haven't seen her.

"When she reached London, she told me it was beautiful and she was happy."

Gusharan said her sister was "very intelligent".

"She was the top of her class here in India when she was studying, she's a very hard worker. She loved us all very much.

"Our family is very poor. She always thinks about us first. She was very supportive to me. She was my world. My heart hurts."

Half-time at the World Cup final lasted 27 minutes and 19 seconds after the ‘Super Bowl style’ show delayed the resumption of the match between Argentina and Spain.

Organisers Fifa had assured both teams before the final that the half-time show, curated by Coldplay’s Chris Martin and featuring Madonna, Shakira, BTS, Justin Bieber and Burna Boy, would only last 11 minutes, with the time needed to assemble and dismantle the stage at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey taking the total length of the expected break to around 20 minutes.

However, the delay to the World Cup final was actually much longer, which meant Fifa went even further in breaking their own rules. The half-time show also brought cameos from Brazil legends Ronaldo and Ronaldinho, Ted Lasso actor Jason Sudeikis, as well as Kermit the Frog and Miss Piggy. Appearing on the BBC, former England captain Wayne Rooney said it was “crap”.

open image in gallery Lionel Messi’s Argentina faced a 27-minute delay before resuming the World Cup final ( Getty )

In the laws of the game, governed by Ifab (the International Football Association Board), it states half-time breaks should “not exceed 15 minutes”. There were over 27 minutes between referee Slavko Vincic’s whistle at the end of the first half and the start of the second.

There was a precedent set from last year’s Club World Cup final between eventual winners Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain, which was also organised by Fifa and held in the same venue in New Jersey. That show lasted 24 minutes, with Coldplay, J Balvin, Doja Cat, Tems and Emmanuel Kelly featuring.

Additionally, the 2024 Copa America final between Argentina and Colombia in Miami, organised by South American confederation Conmebol and featuring a performance from Shakira, lasted 25 minutes.

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

There were warnings that an extended World Cup half-time break could lead to an increased risk of injuries. Dr Liam Harper, a senior lecturer in physiology at Manchester Metropolitan University’s Institute of Sport, told the Press Association that reduction in muscle temperature "will be potentially more pronounced” due to an extended break.

The World Cup final also kicked off six minutes late, following performance by Robbie Williams, the singing of the national anthem by Jennifer Hudson, a bizarre pre-game speech by actor Tom Cruise, and a ‘let’s get ready to rumble’ build-up by ring announcers the Buffer brothers - Michael and Bruce.

News.title: Spain v Argentina LIVE: Tense World Cup final resumes after polarising half-time show
News.content:
Madonna joined by Ronaldo and Ronaldinho for entrance to World Cup half-time performance

Footballing giants Argentina and Spain are clashing in a blockbuster World Cup final, as Lionel Messi graces this stage for perhaps the final time.

A dismal, goalless first half at New York New Jersey Stadium saw no real chances for either side with ITV pundit Ian Wright blaming the pitch, saying “it's ridiculous, it's poor, it's terrible,” and describing it as “bobbly and dry”. A lengthy half-time show then ensured the interval lasted for more than 27 minutes, with BBC pundit Wayne Rooney particularly unimpressed, describing the spectacle as “crap”.

All-time great Messi, 39, is looking to lead Argentina – who broke English hearts by coming from behind to win their semi-final – to a second straight World Cup trophy and the nation’s fourth overall, after triumphs in 1978, 1986 and 2022.

But they face formidable foes in the reigning European champions: Spain, who are seeking their second-ever world championship, having previously lifted the trophy in 2010. La Roja were superb as they downed France with a clinical 2-0 win in the last four and also have 19-year-old star Lamine Yamal in their ranks, a winger who can change any game in an instant.

Brazil legends Ronaldo and Ronaldinho joined Madonna in an extraordinary World Cup 2026 final half-time show.

The Selecao icons were seen driving into the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on a cart, with Madonna kicking off the show after Spain and Argentina played out a 0-0 draw in the first half.

The two former Brazil players have been seen at various Fifa World Cup 2026 matches, even outside of their own nation’s games, with Carlo Ancelotti’s side exiting the tournament at the hands of Norway in the last 16.

But Ronaldo and Ronaldinho were both greeted with cheers from the sell-out crowd as they entered the pitch, with the pair celebrated over recent weeks as previous winners of the tournament from 2002.

open image in gallery Ronaldinho and Ronaldo with Madonna during the half time show during the FIFA World Cup 2026 final ( PA )

ITV Sport’s Ian Wright noted how “Ronaldinho’s tracksuit looked massive,” with the reviews of the show overall mixed across social media.

Wayne Rooney described the show as “crap” on the BBC’s coverage, while Gary Neville said he “enjoyed it,” with ITV Sport colleague Wright claiming that Burna Boy “saved it” with his performance alongside Shakira.

open image in gallery Former Brazil football players Ronaldinho and Ronaldo with Madonna during the half time show ( Reuters )

But Roy Keane was also underwhelmed: “It was a bit of an anti-climax, but listen, it’s so nice to see Shakira.”

After Madonna concluded her segment, the half-time show then moved on to feature Justin Bieber, who performed an acoustic version of ‘Everything Hallelujah’.

Shakira and Burna Boy then performed their official World Cup anthem ‘Dai, Dai’.

open image in gallery Former Brazil players Ronaldo and Ronaldinho during the halftime show ( Reuters )

Coldplay’s Chris Martin curated the show, which extended well beyond the customary 15-minute interval for official Fifa matches, according to IFAB, coming in at 27 minutes and 19 seconds.

The half-time show has created controversy for Fifa, who have shifted the structure of the sport during the tournament, including hydration breaks to divide each half into two intervals, much like American sports.

News.content:

Fire crews are fighting a blaze that broke out at Arthur’s Seat in Edinburgh on Sunday evening.

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service (SFRS) has four appliances at the scene after responding to reports of the fire at 6.38pm.

It came as SFRS continued to battle a wildfire in the Cairngorms, which has been burning since Wednesday.

A spokesperson said: “We were alerted at 6.38pm on Sunday 19 July to reports of a fire in the open at Arthur’s Seat in Edinburgh.

“Operations Control mobilised four fire appliances and crews are still at the scene.

“There are no reported casualties.”

Earlier on Sunday Cairngorms park officials said the large-scale wildfire affecting the region is now “largely surrounded”, and expect evacuated residents to be able to return home “later today”.

On Sunday afternoon, park bosses said the fire, which burnt around four square kilometres at its peak, is largely under control.

The park authority announced that the incident remains ongoing, nevertheless, with fire crews and other partners tackling the blaze together.

Park bosses said resources, including helicopter support, have been integral in battling the fire in tougher-to-reach areas.

Gavin Miles, director of planning and place at the park authority, said: “News from Glenmore this morning is very encouraging, with colleagues from SFRS indicating that the fire is now largely surrounded. This is, though, still a live situation and teams are still very active on the ground, so we are taking nothing for granted at this stage.

“We’re really grateful for the continued efforts of everyone helping fight the fire in Glenmore, and for the co-operation of local residents, visitors and businesses at what I know is a very difficult time.

“The Ski Road and surrounding areas are likely to be off-limits for some time to come, given the sheer number of people and machinery on-site, but we’re hopeful that residents and campers directly impacted by the exclusion zone will be able to gain access later today.”

Harry Brook paid tribute to England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum after they claimed a first ODI series victory over India since 2018 with a 27-run win at Lord’s.

McCullum lost his Test job earlier this month after a home defeat to New Zealand, but has bounced back with England able to achieve a superb 4-0 T20 series victory over world champions India which was followed by a precious triumph in the 50-over format.

Ben Duckett’s masterful 141 proved the bedrock of a record-breaking total of 387 for three, a new best ever List A score at Lord’s with 91 for new ODI opener Jacob Bethell along with late contributions from Joe Root, who made 74 not out, and Jos Buttler’s sparkling 13-ball innings of 41 crucial.

It earned England a handsome halfway advantage of this winner-takes-all contest, but Rohit Sharma put retirement rumours to bed with an equally stunning 138 to become the first India player to score an ODI hundred at this historic venue.

open image in gallery England claimed ODI success against India after a thrilling Lord’s finale (Steven Paston/PA) ( PA Wire )

However, Brook’s decision to turn to Bethell’s part-time spin proved inspired with the Barbados-born youngster able to bowl Sharma on a day where tributes were paid to his old mentor Sir Garfield Sobers, who died on Friday.

Sam Curran then struck twice in the 44th over before Virat Kohli departed for 74 to help restrict India to 360 for seven, but Brook placed the credit for Bethell’s unexpected spell of one for 49 to the much-maligned McCullum, who guided England to only a second ODI series win over India since 2012.

“That was a tough little period, they were obviously getting ahead of the game and playing really well. I decided to go off for an over and have a quick chat with Baz to gather his thoughts,” Brook said.

“Again, it comes back to the communication which has been outstanding throughout the T20s, throughout the ODIs.

“They have a slightly different view from up there, with the TVs and analytic work and going up there to have a quick chat to see what we could do. He said, ‘have a go with Beth, a slightly different spinner to what we’ve got with him driving it into the pitch,’ and thankfully it came off.

“Yeah, extremely pleased with the way we have performed throughout the whole series, going 1-0 down and the fight and camaraderie and belief to win 2-1 in the end, like we did in Sri Lanka, I think it’s a credit to the team, the coaches and an outstanding performance.”

With England on the hunt for a new Test head coach and captain after the departures of McCullum and Ben Stokes respectively, Brook did his chances no harm with six wins across seven completed white-ball matches.

Yet, Brook acknowledged it would be “tough” to juggle all formats ahead of a 2027 where a home Ashes series is followed by an ODI World Cup in South Africa.

open image in gallery Harry Brook admits juggling all three formats as captain would be difficult (Steven Paston/PA) ( PA Wire )

Brook added: “That’s not my decision. Whoever is the new coach will have that decision to make. It would be tough to do it, but I’m not saying it is impossible. If I get asked, we’ll see where it takes us.”

India captain Shubman Gill felt the late hitting of Buttler proved decisive, especially without the injured Jasprit Bumrah before he side-stepped questions about Sharma, who batted majestically after 24 hours of rumours it could be his final innings.

On Sharma, Gill said: “I mean he has not told us anything. I think it is all out in the media, but there has not been any discussions internally.

“Our bowling is a little inexperienced and we were put under the pump in this match and we didn’t respond.”

News.title: Ryan Fox matches father Grant’s sporting folklore with Claret Jug
News.content:
It’s the final day of the Open Championship, golf’s oldest and most-prestigious major. The leaderboard offers up hope of a seesaw day where little-known-of golfers tussle it out with big names under the north-west English sun. All in all, it should be an exciting day.

But, as with the past two days, we head into the round with talk dominated by a certain Bryson DeChambeau. It’s as frustrating and annoying as it is, in these days dominated by social media/content etc etc, painfully predictable. So let’s get the DeChambeau news out the way. Having been fairly hit with a two-shot penalty for improving his lie on Friday, the YouTube content creator had a tantrum, threatened to withdraw, caused a delay in the release of third-round tee times, before turning up and shooting a one-under 69 to lie four behind the leader heading into today.

That’s not all, The Bryson DeChambeau Show carried on after yesterday’s round where James Corrigan takes up the script...

Bryson DeChambeau marched straight to the offices of the R&A after being heckled with a cry of “you’re a cheat” on Birkdale’s 18th green on Saturday. As the controversy over his two-shot penalty from Friday’s second round rumbled on, Telegraph Sport understands DeChambeau, who shot a third-round 69 to lie four shots off the lead of the Open, asked R&A chief executive Mark Darbon for his scorecard from Friday. It is against policy so his request was rejected. DeChambeau then went back to the recorder’s hut and asked if they had it. Again, the answer was in the negative. It is unclear why he wanted it, but a theory emerged that he wished to put it on his social media channels.

All in all it is pathetic posturing that you’d expect from a stroppy teenager. He’s only three off the lead and has the game to win at Royal Birkdale, he’d do well to forget the perceived slights (whatever they may be) and get on with trying to win the Claret Jug.

Oh, and to add another scene to the soap opera Rory McIlroy doubtless spoke for many inside and outside the rope when he called out DeChambeau saying: “Yeah, look, I won’t pretend to be up here and defend Bryson. I’m not particularly fond of him. I think a lot of it’s performative. I think a lot of it’s for attention. To hold the tournament hostage like that, and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn’t feel like it was a great look.”

So, I think it’s best we focus on the golf today and not the theatrics and sorry antics of the American.

Sam Burns, his playing partner yesterday, was brilliant as he backed up his 62 of Friday with a five-under 65. He leads by two on 10 under and is the man to beat. Lurking behind with intent are a host of big names and big hitters – Ryan Fox (eight under), Si Woo Kim (eight under), Lucas Herbert (six under), Ludvig Aberg (seven under) and the man himself YouTube’s very own DeChambeau (six under).

Also in with a hint of a hope is Tommy Fleetwood, the hometown boy in search of his first major, the Englishman will start the round on five under.

Stay here for all the action, where I hope all the talk during and after the day’s round is focused on the winner’s brilliance rather than the emotions of DeChambeau.

News.title: Records tumble at Lord’s as England win thriller against India
News.content:
When he fell, bowled trying to sweep Bethell, India were 260 for two, still a tough ask but not impossible, especially against an England side with plenty of demons. Kohli fired up in Rohit’s absence, hitting Will Jacks for two sixes and Bethell into the pavilion.

But the run-rate faltered as Curran whipped out his slower-ball bag of tricks. He had Ishan Kishan and Shreyas Iyer caught in the deep by sub Rehan Ahmed in the 44th over and Kohli in the next, slapping a catch to cover. The rest subsided, India short in the end at 360 for seven.

England’s ODI side have struggled for runs under Brendon McCullum and this was easily their best batting performance, not just for the collection of records but for the calm, controlled way they went about setting a huge total. The openers Duckett and Bethell gave them a 192-run cushion, Root was impregnable again and Buttler finished it off, proving what he can do when others give him a platform. India were without Jasprit Bumrah but that should not take the shine off England’s achievements.

This was the first Duckett-Bethell opening contribution and it was England’s highest for the first wicket since the last World Cup. Jason Roy and Jonny Bairstow were such an important part of the route to World Cup glory and they left a huge hole in the side. Duckett and Bethell are more touch players, capable of gear shifts rather than setting out at turbo pace like Roy and Bairstow. The fact they bat so often together in Test cricket, where Bethell appears at No 3, helps the level of understanding.

Duckett’s innings knocked Viv Richards’s 138 in the 1979 World Cup final off the top spot at Lord’s and continued the form he showed at the end of the New Zealand Test series when he scored his first Test hundred in nearly a year. He was out first ball in the second ODI in Cardiff but was never in any real bother at Lord’s as he compiled a fourth century in this format.

News.title: Antonelli wins Belgian Grand Prix to extend championship lead after Russell crashes out
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix from Spa-Francorchamps. The story of yesterday and in fact the weekend was of everyone trying to dislodge Kimi Antonelli from the top of the timesheets. Spoiler alert if you did not watch qualifying: they failed.

That is not to say the fight wasn’t a half-decent one. Max Verstappen and Red Bull were the closest challengers in the end, demonstrating an element of revival during a tricky season. Whether that will continue during the race is hard to know. Verstappen certainly thought he would have been further down the field without the tremendous tow he received from Isack Hadjar, his Red Bull team-mate, in the final sector.

Lando Norris also pushed Verstappen, though was almost half a second down on Antonelli’s time in the end. Unfortunately he will not be able to take advantage of a start from third place because he takes a 10-place grid penalty. George Russell, who has managed to reduce his Mercedes team-mate’s advantage to just 25 points in the past few rounds, was fourth and will start third. He did however, have a difficult session once again, finishing more than half a second off his team-mate.

He was at a loss to explain this. Well, he knows where he lost most of the time: on the straights. But he still does not understand exactly why it is happening. The good news for him is that third place is often the most optimal starting position at this track.

Will that be the case today? Let’s see...

News.title: England win gives Borthwick breathing space after late try controversy
News.content:
And in doing so he may have just saved Borthwick’s job.

The Rugby Football Union, following its review into England’s Six Nations campaign that yielded just one victory, had publicly offered its backing to its head coach through to the World Cup. But in reality, there are no guarantees. It needed evidence of England’s progress.

Two wins from three rounds of the Nations Championship is likely to convince RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney to back his man. But Borthwick will know that nothing can be taken for granted.

Four years ago, Eddie Jones, facing similar scrutiny from his employers, looked to have salvaged his job by winning the last two matches in a three-Test summer tour of Australia. But it did still not save him from the sack the following November.

Still. There was enough character and attacking prowess to convince the RFU that, despite the flaws in this display, the team are on the right track again.

It was still far from an 80-minute performance, but this was England’s first away victory in a year, in a hostile environment and after all the challenges, both physical and mental, the players have faced in travelling to three continents over three weeks – clocking up more than 25,000 miles – at the end of a long season.

England wobbled alarmingly earlier in the second half but remarkably found the resilience to drag themselves back into the game just as it looked like it was slipping from their grasp. That is clear evidence of players playing for their coach and each other.

Discipline, however, remains a major problem for Borthwick’s England. They had been cruising to what would looked to have been a statement victory at half-time following tries by Tommy Freeman and two by Ben Earl, in what had been their finest half of rugby this year.

And yet, once again indiscipline undermined their efforts. Remarkably, they were shown four yellow cards – Jack van Poortvliet, Alex Coles, Pollock (to more booing) and Emmanuel Iyogun – in the second half to take their total to 14 in their last 10 Tests, and at one stage were down to 12 men but, significantly, this time it did not prove fatal.
