News.title: Tuchel learns lesson as England clinch third place in 10-goal thriller
News.content:
Neither England nor France wanted to be playing this game in Miami, but they can have no complaints about the nature of their semi-final defeats.

Tournament favourites France were comprehensively outplayed by Spain, with their feted front four of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Bradley Barcola and Michael Olise all turning in below-par performances.

England’s defeat by Argentina was perhaps not as much of a surprise, but the nature of Thomas Tuchel’s team’s second-half collapse was just as alarming as France’s no-show.

England’s manager was fiercely criticised for replacing Anthony Gordon with Ezri Konsa and switching to a back five in the 72nd minute, but Tuchel has since defended his decisions.

“If you are asking if I regret my decisions, if this is the question, then I say no. I don’t regret my ‌decisions because I ‌felt that we became ⁠too passive,” said Tuchel.

“I took several decisions, trusting my instinct, my intuition, my experience, trusting my competitiveness, and I took the decision in order to help the team and get the result.

“I would regret if I didn’t help. I would regret ⁠if we didn’t react, but I have no regrets over the decision itself.”

Quite how strong Didier Deschamps and Tuchel decide to go with their teams is anyone’s guess. There has been some suggestion that Mbappe will start to give him the chance to beat Lionel Messi to the Golden Boot.

Some of England’s regular starters, such as Declan Rice, look physically spent, so there could be some rotation, and even a chance for players such as Kobbie Mainoo who has not played a minute of football at the tournament.

The third/fourth-place play-off has been rebranded as the “Bronze Final” for this tournament, and Tuchel was keen to point out that finishing third would be England’s best World Cup result since 1966. They lost this fixture against Belgium in 2018, but the way that game has been widely forgotten speaks volumes.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Scotland fight back to claim victory against Fiji in Nations Championship
News.content:
A barrelling Schoeman finished an initial break by match captain Stafford McDowall, then Dobie burrowed over beside the posts in the 61st minute to put Scotland in front for the first time in 40 minutes.

Scotland glossed up the scoreline with two more tries in the last six minutes by Cummings and Dobie again to send home a crowd of 55,000 happy.

“I thought our bench did really well,” Townsend told the BBC. “Something I’ve learned over the last 12 months, the bench can help you change momentum. The players can come up with solutions themselves but the bench can give you energy and solutions but also bravery. We’re a team that will back our decisions and that put real pressure on Fiji.

“I felt [Fiji] picked their strongest side today and it took a lot of work for us to break them down but also it took a really good defensive performance,” Townsend added. “Fiji didn’t really break us that often [and] in that final quarter the guys were outstanding. We’ll take a few positives from that.”

Fiji had never beaten Scotland at Murrayfield but would have sensed the chance of making history by half-time. The Fijians were tough and clinical in a huge turnaround from last weekend when they were humiliated by England 73-8 in Liverpool.

News.title: Hometown hero Tommy Fleetwood facing tough ask to end 57 years of Open hurt
News.content:
Never mind Bryson DeChambeau stomping around in the rough as he improved his lie, for so long this Open Saturday turned into Tommy Fleetwood walking in his Royal Birkdale wonderland as he enhanced the mood of seemingly everyone in attendance.

Alas, the fun could not last and, even though he still has a chance of becoming England’s first Open winner on English soil since 1969, that finish looked costly. Fifty-seven years of hurt and all that...

On five under, Fleetwood is in a tie for ninth, five off the lead held by Sam Burns, the American who, after a 65, is two clear of New Zealander Ryan Fox and South Korean Kim Si-woo. DeChambeau is alongside Swede Ludvig Aberg, in a tie for sixth on six under, after a 69.

He was heckled on the 18th because of the two-shot penalty he received on Friday night for “inadvertently improving his lie” on the fifth. “You’re a cheat, Bryson,” the fan shouted.

It was a sour point that was in no way in keeping with the mood of this Saturday that had been overwhelmingly positive. With Fleetwood as the focus, of course.

The enormous crowd cheered and sang and backed their fellow Merseysider all the way as Fleetwood launched his charge into contention at this Southport links which he would once sneak on as a child. His playing partner, Jon Rahm, was taken aback by the level of support.

“The best way I can explain it, it was so intense that, without meaning any disrespect I’m glad England didn’t win the semi-final [of the World Cup] because I would have been having a heck of a three days with the fans if they had been playing Spain in tomorrow’s final,” Rahm said.

Sports.title: Gary Lineker’s son won thousands with stunning seven-fold World Cup final bet
Sports.content:
Gary Lineker’s son won thousands with stunning seven-fold World Cup final bet

George Lineker will be hoping to repeat the trick when Argentina and Spain clash in Sunday's World Cup final

View Image Gary Lineker's son George landed a monster bet at the World Cup 2022 in Qatar (Image: WireImage)

Gary Lineker was one of England’s greatest World Cup heroes during his playing days. The former Three Lions striker won the Golden Boot at Mexico in 1986 and finished his international career with 10 World Cup goals – a national record that stood for 40 years before Harry Kane finally overtook him earlier this summer.

‌



He is also a familiar face at the tournament as a broadcaster, firstly fronting the BBC’s live coverage for decades and now starring on Netflix with his hugely popular The Rest Is Football podcast. And one of his sons also has a memorable World Cup story to tell as well.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The 2022 final in Qatar is widely regarded as one of the greatest matches in football history, with Lionel Messi inspiring Argentina to victory over France after an extraordinary 3-3 draw that featured a Kylian Mbappe hat-trick before a dramatic penalty shootout. It also proved unforgettable for Gary’s eldest son, George, who landed a sizeable four-figure payout after placing an ambitious seven-fold accumulator on the match.

The 34-year-old entrepreneur staked just £20.03 at odds of 170/1, walking away with a tidy return of £4,276.40. George correctly predicted that both Messi and Mbappe would find the net, while also backing the score to be 2-2 after 90 minutes.

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

‌



He also successfully tipped Argentina to lift the trophy on penalties, with his remaining selections centred on the total number of corners and yellow cards shown during the match. Sharing the winning bet slip on social media, he joked: “If anyone deserves to win a bet, I think it’s me. Thank you all.”

Gary Lineker appears on BBC high earners list despite quitting over a year ago READ MORE :

“Haha…you were due one. Congrats mate,” replied Piers Morgan, while his son Spencer quipped: “The only good thing to come out of this.”

That triumph in Qatar finally completed Messi’s glittering career, with the Argentina captain finally lifting the one major trophy that had previously eluded him. Widely regarded as the greatest footballer of all time, the 39-year-old now has the chance to make even more history by becoming a back-to-back World Cup winner.

‌

Argentina booked their place in Sunday’s final after a dramatic comeback victory over England on Wednesday evening, with Messi pulling the strings once again by providing two crucial assists. George Lineker will no doubt be hoping lightning strikes twice as he looks to land another money-spinning World Cup final punt.

Gary Lineker makes instant England prediction after France and responds to Bukayo Saka

Gary Lineker has made an early prediction for England ahead of Euro 2028

View 2 Images Former England star Gary Lineker has had his say on the Three Lions' hopes for Euro 2028. (Image: The Rest Is Football.)

Gary Lineker believes England can go and win Euro 2028 after they demolished France in their third place match in Miami. England hammered Les Bleus 6-4 in a surprising end to the Three Lions' World Cup campaign, claiming the bronze medal and their best ever finish at a World Cup since winning the tournament in 1966.

‌



Speaking on The Rest Is Football podcast, Lineker said: "I told you this was the game we'd all been waiting for. England have put six past France and finished third at the World Cup, confirming their best ever performance since 1966.

‌



"It was a good way for England to finish the tournament. It felt a bit like a testamonial game, but all in all, it was actually very entertaining.

‌



World Cup final chaos as furious fans forced to wait HOURS to enter stadium READ MORE :

Arsenal eye shock transfer for England World Cup hero after Morgan Rogers snub READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"To be honest, after the levels of that performance , it's hard not to see us winning the Euros." Lineker burst into laughter after the remark and Micah Richards told his fellow presenter to 'stop it.'

One of the major talking points after the game was Bukayo Saka and his absence from the England starting XI in the semi-final defeat to Argentina, scoring a hat-trick in the demolition job on France.

‌



Speaking after the game, Saka made it clear that he wasn't injured and was fully fit, with Thomas Tuchel admitting he felt obliged to manage the Arsenal man's minutes having struggled with injuries.

"Of course, I would love to have played more," Saka told the BBC after the game. "But of course, it's not the time to talk about out that now. I try to do my talking on the pitch. It's done now. Move on."

When asked if he was fully fit, the Arsenal winger replied: "Yeah. I'm fit. I'm fit."

‌



View 2 Images Bukayo Saka spoke after netting a hat-trick (Image: FIFA)

Lineker asked his panel on the Rest is Football: "What about Saka? He got a hat-trick but he didn't play a minute in the semi-final. You thought, if he's protecting him then he won't play a minute in the third-place game.

"But he does and he scores an excellent hattrick. What do you think?"

‌



"I understand why Tuchel played Rogers in that game," Richards replied. "For the transition, but for him not to come on, talking about Saka and his fitness, his and Rice's fitness all tournament has been a question.

"But for him not to feature, is just bizarre and I can't get my head around why."

"You know when he's been on the pitch," Lineker interjected. "He's got a goal and an assist every 59 minutes that he's played. Three goals and three assists."

Article continues below

Richards replied: "The thing is about Saka, he gets you fouls as well and he gets you up the pitch. How many times have we seen him going up the pitch and he puts his arm out and buys a foul?"

Alan Shearer also weighed in, saying:: "We were always told he wasn't quite right, that he wasn't 100 per cent fit. If he wasn't fit then he wasn't going to start him.

"It was strange he never came on in the semi-final and then to start today. It was brilliant for him to score a hattrick."

Sports.title: Donald Trump picks his World Cup winner and makes request to Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
Donald Trump picks his World Cup winner and makes request to Gianni Infantino

Spain are set to play against Argentina in the World Cup final at 8pm on Sunday evening, with Donald Trump picking who will win FIFA's most prestigious tournament

View Image Donald Trump believes Argentina will win the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

Donald Trump has predicted that Argentina will win the 2026 World Cup final, with the US President saying "It's hard to bet against [Lionel] Messi." Trump will have the best seat in the house as the South Americans take on Spain at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on Sunday evening at 8pm.

‌



Trump will also present the World Cup trophy to the winning team in the aftermath of the final. However, in the build-up to the match, Trump was probed by the American broadcaster FOX on who he believes will win - the European champions or the defending World Cup titleholders.

‌



He reflected on Messi's semi-final winning assist against England as he said: "I watched that pass...I guess you’d call it a pass...that was perfect.

‌

Trump also had a special request for Gianni Infantino, as he urged the FIFA president to return to the USA for the next instalment of world football's most prestigious competition. He explained: "I had a great idea for Gianni.

‌



"I said, 'You have to do two countries - so announce us for next time, and then announce another country after that and it’ll take out some of the anger and the shock.'

Sports.title: Harry Kane reveals England dressing room's verdict on Thomas Tuchel amid fan frustration
Sports.content:
Harry Kane reveals England dressing room's verdict on Thomas Tuchel amid fan frustration

Thomas Tuchel's name was booed by England fans when it was announced over the PA system before his side ended their World Cup campaign with an entertaining 6-4 win against France to clinch third place

View 3 Images Harry Kane is firmly behind Thomas Tuchel (Image: ITV)

Harry Kane insists England’s players are fully behind Thomas Tuchel even after their World Cup heartbreak. Kane insists Tuchel’s “enthusiasm and tactical experience” can carry England forward even if the captain admitted they are still in the “grieving stage.”

‌



Three Lions striker Kane also said fans have a right to be “sad and angry” at the way they lost the semi-final to Argentina and it will take time to get over the disappointment. England did at least achieve their best World Cup finish on foreign soil as they beat France to get the bronze medal and Kane says it is hard to swallow because boss Tuchel allowed them all to dream.

‌



Kane said: “It’s our highest finish in 60 years. The enthusiasm he has, the emotion he brings, the tactical experience he has. It doesn’t mean you’re going to get it right every time.

‌



“We want to get it right on the biggest occasions and he expects that from himself as well. He’s a fantastic coach. He not only gave the players belief but he gave the country belief that it was our year.

Get the latest World Cup 2026 news in your inbox with our Make Football Great Again newsletter

Harry Kane's sad admission to England teammates spotted by lip reader after France win READ MORE :

“That is why it hurts even more than other years because everyone believed we were going all the way. Everyone has to process it. He has to process it himself.

‌



“We’re still in that grieving stage, the emotional stage, and we’ll be in that for the next few weeks. It won’t be until the next camp where you think about what the future holds and what the next target is. We’ll have conversations as captain and manager and with other team mates and staff, to see where we can be better.”

Kane admitted he can understand the fans’ frustrations and Tuchel’s name was even booed before kick-off in the third-place play-off game with France. Kane said: “It’s so hard. I think the fans are behind the team and are behind the manager.

Should the FA keep Thomas Tuchel in charge? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel's name was booed by England fans (Image: CHANDAN KHANNA/AFP via Getty Images)

“When something like this happens it’s very emotional – and rightly so. We’ve all been England fans when we wished we’d done this or that and it didn’t quite happen. That will die down naturally.

“Before we know it, we’ll be back with our clubs and the focus shifts to Champions League or the Nations League. Things do move quickly. Fans have a right to be emotional, sad and angry. We all are, we all feel it.

‌



“We have a chance to change it but it wasn’t to be this year. There is still a lot of positives to take from this, competing against the odds away from home and you finish third. Keep your chin up and go again.

“When you take the job of England manager, he knows that if it doesn’t go the way we want it then he’s going to take some stick. That is part and parcel of the job. I know there are a lot of questions after the other night. We have to process it as players. I’m sure the manager will.

View 3 Images Harry Kane and Thomas Tuchel have formed a good relationship (Image: Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images)

‌



“It’s his first major tournament. He’ll learn a lot from the players, the situations, the pressures, the travel. There are also a lot of things as players we can learn from the other night. For now it’s just trying to process everything.

“We had a lot of good things, a lot of tough situations we overcame. The group is incredible, the best England group I’ve been a part of in terms of togetherness. The boss was a big part of creating that as well.”

Sports.title: 'My hands were all over the place!' - Fox savours dramatic Open win
Sports.content:
Ryan Fox admitted it was a "dream come true" as he defied the nerves to clinch a dramatic victory in The Open at Royal Birkdale.

The 39-year-old New Zealander produced a superb finish to the final round to overtake clubhouse leader Cameron Young and snatch a one-shot win.

Fox, who had carded a 62 on Saturday to put himself in contention to claim a maiden major success, looked to be slipping out of it after making his second bogey of the day at the 11th.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the final round of the 154th Open as Fox claimed the victory

Back-to-back birdies at the 13th and 14th put him back in the hunt and he then did well to escape with only a bogey at the 15th after a nightmare lie in a greenside bunker.

He hit back by birdieing the 16th following a brilliant approach and then, after missing a chance at the 17th, nailed two superb shots down the 18th before boldly draining a 12-foot putt to claim the Claret Jug.

"To play that last hole how I did, I stood on the tee and said to my caddie Dean (Smith), we're going to try to win this," said Fox.

"I hit two perfect shots. I'm not sure how I hit the putt. My hands were all over the place. I was just trying to get it towards the hole somewhere. It's surreal that it went in.

"My focus with the putter all day was just take a really deep breath before I hit it and just try to hit a line, and I did that.

Image: Fox celebrates after holing the winning putt

"I don't know how I managed to keep the putter face square enough for that to go on line, but I'll take it.

"Champion Golfer of the Year has got a pretty good ring to it. It is a dream come true.

"You do dream of this moment. I don't know whether I ever thought it was going to become a reality. Now it is, and to have my name etched in the history of the game is pretty awesome. I think it's pretty awesome for New Zealand as well. It's going to be big down there."

Fox is the son of former All Blacks fly-half Grant Fox and the grandson of former New Zealand Test captain Merv Wallace.

"We've got a great history in our family," he said. "I was lucky enough to carve my own path there. I don't know if this tops their achievements, but it's certainly right up there.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fox equalled the lowest round in Open history with a third-round 62 at Royal Birkdale

"I spoke to my kids last night, and they said bring back a trophy. I think this is a pretty cool one to bring back for them.

"I don't know if my dad would be able to contain himself when I was coming down the stretch. He's never been one who has been very good if he doesn't have control over things.

"I think when he was playing and in control of the output, under pressure he was fine. But when he doesn't have control, I think he's a nervous wreck. I'm sure he was."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player How Fox clinched victory in The Open at Royal Birkdale

'He stayed aggressive'

Sky Sports Golf duo Dame Laura Davies and Andrew Coltart were both full of praise for Fox and the aggressive approach he adopted on the back nine.

Davies said: "He was the most impressive player all day. He stayed aggressive; I don't think he was scared of losing it. If he lost it because he hit a shot that just didn't work out he was prepared to stay aggressive and I firmly believe that's why he did it.

"He hit irons when he had to, but when there was a chance, a sniff of a birdie, the driver was out, full commitment.

"And the way he played 18 I don't think you could have drawn that up any better. Two of the best shots he will ever hit in his life just to hit that green to give himself a chance."

Image: Fox proudly holds the Claret Jug

Coltart added: "I've never seen somebody push through the tape as hard as that right at the end of the tournament to win a major championship.

"At a place like this, too. It was just superb. The 62 on Saturday I think, helped cement his belief in his ability out there.

"While they all struggled with the pressure, he stood tall."

What's next?

Sports.title: 'My heart really sank' - Hamilton relieved mechanic unhurt after hit
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says his "heart really sank" when his Ferrari car hit a mechanic in a pit stop in an incident that saw the team fined heavily by Belgian Grand Prix stewards.

Hamilton's right-front tyre struck the mechanic after the driver was given the green signal to leave the team's pit box, briefly knocking the crew member - who was in front of the wheel in an attempt to make a front-wing adjustment - to his knees.

Hamilton promptly stopped his car as the mechanic, who was unhurt, was helped to his feet before leaving the pit box.

The incident was placed under a post-race stewards' investigation with Ferrari later handed a €30,000 fine, €10,000 of which is suspended for a year.

With no sporting sanction imposed on the driver, who stewards said had suffered a "sporting disadvantage" already due to the fact he was delayed in leaving the pit stop, Hamilton retained his fourth-place finish in the race.

The result moved Hamilton back into second place ahead of George Russell in the Drivers' Championship with a deficit of 45 points to Kimi Antonelli, the race winner at Spa-Francorchamps.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix.

Speaking about the pit stop confusion after the race, Hamilton said his mind had immediately flashed back to an incident at the 2018 Bahrain Grand Prix when a botched Ferrari stop involving Kimi Raikkonen caused a mechanic, Francesco Cigarini, to suffer a double leg fracture.

Hamilton was therefore relieved when told as he enquired about the mechanic over team radio that he had been unhurt.

"The green light went and so I went," said Hamilton to Sky Sports F1.

"You're looking over here [to the left at the lights] you're not looking over there so that's more probably on the team, ultimately.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Despite being given a five-second penalty for an opening lap collision with George Russell, Lewis Hamilton was left more frustrated with his performance over the weekend as he finished fourth in Belgium.

"But when it happened, then I noticed him and I stopped and it just went through my mind in that moment was back when Kimi hit and broke a leg and my heart really sank for a second.

"I'm really grateful he's ok."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton crashes at Turn 13 during the final practice session at the Belgian GP.

'We could have been challenging for the win' - Hamilton rues consequence of his Saturday crash

Hamilton's stop had already been elongated by the fact that Ferrari's crew had first had to wait five seconds before starting the car's tyre change owing to the serving of a time penalty for causing a collision with Russell at Les Combes on the opening lap.

The clash spun Russell out of the race, although the Mercedes driver later blamed his own car's straight-line speed issues, rather than former team-mate Hamilton, for the incident at the end of the long Kemmel Straight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch from onboard with George Russell as he crashes out of the Belgian GP after contact with Lewis Hamilton.

Hamilton also preferred not to focus on the specifics of the collision in his post-race interview, instead taking the blame for not qualifying higher than sixth, which became fifth on the grid due to Lando Norris' engine penalty, after crashing in Saturday's final practice session.

"I don't count on myself [being] unlucky, I think about my mistake that I made yesterday, so I take full responsibility really for the fourth place that I ended up getting," he said.

"I damaged the car then when they rebuilt the car they missed something on the suspension so the balance was completely different so it meant I was probably a good couple of tenths - maybe three tenths - slower than I should have been in qualifying.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Drama at the start of the Belgium GP as George Russell's title hopes take a huge blow.

"Then I ended up further back, got in the incident. Five second penalty, so like a domino effect from a mistake from myself.

"But the team have been doing a great job with strategy, pit stops. We are continuing to improve the car. I think our pace today, without the damage, we could have been challenging for the win."

Sports.title: Antonelli takes big Belgian GP win as Russell's title woes deepen
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli overcame an unfortunately-timed Virtual Safety Car to overtake Charles Leclerc and win the Belgian Grand Prix on a day team-mate George Russell's title hopes suffered a major fresh setback.

Antonelli doubled his in-house advantage over Russell to 50 points after the Briton was spun out into the gravel at the fifth corner of the first lap in a collision with Lewis Hamilton that stewards judged the Ferrari driver at fault for.

Hamilton was given a five-second penalty, which he served at his sole pit stop, and eventually finished fourth after overtaking McLaren's Oscar Piastri with four laps to go.

Hamilton and Ferrari faced a post-race investigation for an unsafe Ferrari release at the same pit stop.

A mechanic was struck by the Ferrari's front-right tyre and was briefly knocked to his knees after Hamilton was incorrectly given the signal to leave his pit box. The mechanic was unhurt.

Ferrari were fined €30,000, of which a third of the amount was suspended for 12 months, for the incident.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Ferrari pit crew were unable to adjust Lewis Hamilton's front wing as the British driver knocked over a mechanic after being given the green light

Hamilton moves back ahead of Russell to second behind Antonelli in the standings - 45 points behind the Italian, whose sixth victory of the season reinforces his championship favourite status with one race to go in Hungary this coming week before Formula 1's summer break after Mercedes unreliability had struck his car in two of the previous three races.

Max Verstappen, who briefly took the lead from Antonelli on the first lap into Eau Rouge before the Mercedes almost immediately blasted back past, took third after he was also jumped by Leclerc during the VSC.

The Dutchman struggled on the hard tyres in the final stint and finished nine seconds behind Leclerc for Red Bull's 300th podium finish in F1.

Isack Hadjar drove strongly to finish sixth in the second Red Bull from the back row, opportunistically making two pit stops under the early Safety Car for Russell's crash to fulfil the mandatory race-tyre requirements.

Hadjar just held off Lando Norris, who was on significantly fresher tyres, after the McLaren had run to lap 30 before making his one pit stop having started a penalised 13th on the grid.

Gabriel Bortoleto was eighth for Audi ahead of Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad and Alpine's Franco Colapinto.

Belgian GP Result: Top 10 1) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



2) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



3) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



4) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



5) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



6) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



7) Lando Norris, McLaren



8) Gabriel Bortoleto, Audi



9) Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls



10) Franco Colapinto, Alpine

How faultless Antonelli was made to win the hard way

Mercedes' world championship leader had been the big favourite to win the race after qualifying on a dominant pole position but the 19-year-old's route to victory on Sunday did not prove quite as straightforward as many had expected across a tense 44 laps of racing at Spa-Francorchamps.

Antonelli had, though, always been braced for a battle to hold on to his lead through the first lap of the race from fellow front-row-starter Verstappen due to the slipstream-friendly nature of the opening part of the undulating, power-sensitive Belgian lap.

He stayed ahead on the short initial run to La Source but, amid different stages of energy deployment, was overtaken by Verstappen as they arrived at the bottom of Eau Rouge.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Drama at the start of the Belgium GP as George Russell's title hopes take a huge blow

But Antonelli had more battery power in hand for the long Kemmel Straight and duly breezed straight back past the Red Bull before the next braking zone of Les Combes.

Leclerc, meanwhile, had made an impressive start from fourth place and passed Verstappen too.

Verstappen got back ahead of the Ferrari for second place on lap six and, impressively so given the pre-race expectations had been that Antonelli would run and hide, managed to keep the leading Mercedes in view. He was less than three seconds behind Antonelli when he pitted first on lap 17.

Antonelli stopped a lap later and stayed ahead of the Red Bull to maintain the net race lead.

But Ferrari had kept both their drivers out for longer and benefitted when, on lap 20, the Virtual Safety Car was initiated for debris on track.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes Kimi Antonelli discusses his Belgian GP win and admits he's in a 'good position' after opening up a 45-point gap in the drivers' standings.

With the cars on circuit forced to run at reduced speed, Ferrari were able to pit their drivers simultaneously while losing less race time compared to a non-VSC stop.

It worked a treat as Leclerc had jumped both Verstappen and Antonelli on his return to the circuit.

However, Hamilton, who first had to serve his five-second penalty before his tyre change could commence, was further delayed when confusion led to the mechanic who had been asked to adjust his front wing being knocked over when the Briton incorrectly got the green light to leave the box.

Leclerc re-emerged 2.5 seconds ahead of Antonelli and with the apparent advantage of slightly fresher hard tyres.

But the Mercedes simply had too much speed and, unlike two weeks before at Silverstone when the Silver Arrow ran into technical trouble just as it appeared poised to overtake the Ferrari for the lead, Antonelli on lap 34 moved ahead of Leclerc down the Kemmel Straight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oscar Piastri takes to his McLaren team radio to complain about contact with Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.

Not that Mercedes simply breezed away from Ferrari thereafter, Antonelli eventually taking the chequered flag just 1.9s ahead of Leclerc to secure a narrow but significant win given the context of both his recent misfortune and Russell's early exit here.

"It's great to be back on the top step after obviously a few difficult rounds," said Antonelli. "It was a hard-fought race. We lost first place with a VSC but then we managed to make our way back.

"It was a tough win because Charles was quick and we had to hold onto them."

Second place followed Leclerc's victory at Silverstone amid a resurgence in his form, and the Monegasque said: "I believed in the win until the end. We had a little bit of luck with the VSC at the right time for us but the pace was relatively strong.

"There were five or six laps on the hard tyres when I was struggling with the front axle, then it came back a little bit."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell pointed to an issue with the car as a reason for his collision with Lewis Hamilton during the Belgian GP

Russell bemoans Mercedes straight-line speed issues after Hamilton tangle

Race day could barely have gone any worse for a frustrated Russell in the other title-contending Mercedes car.

The Briton had qualified third, a position he held until the Kemmel Straight on lap one when both Ferraris drafted past him and he came under attack from Piastri's McLaren too.

Russell attempted to come back at Hamilton on the outside of his compatriot under braking for the right-handed turn into Les Combes, but the Ferrari understeered and tagged the Mercedes' right-rear wheel, spinning it round into the gravel.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch from onboard with George Russell as he crashes out of the Belgian GP after contact with Lewis Hamilton.

Stewards may have penalised Hamilton for the incident, but Russell instead took issue with the mysterious straight-line speed issues that had dogged his Mercedes all weekend.

"I just got totally swallowed up down the straight," said a dejected Russell.

"I lost three positions down the straight down into Turn Five and then the incident was a racing incident.

"Maybe I could have gone a bit wider, maybe he (Hamilton) could have braked a bit more. The incident shouldn't have happened if I had the speed down the straight."

Sports.title: Duckett, Curran the difference as England clinch India series in Lord's run-fest
Sports.content:
Ben Duckett's century and Sam Curran's late burst of wickets inspired England to a series-clinching 27-run win over India in the third ODI at Lord's.

Duckett struck a magnificent 141 from 135 balls, the highest individual ODI score at Lord's and his fourth century in the format, before a swashbuckling 41 from just 13 balls by Jos Buttler helped England post a daunting 387, setting India 388 to win.

Rohit Sharma led the chase with a superb 138 off 110 deliveries, registering his 34th ODI hundred and sharing century partnerships with Shubman Gill (77) and Virat Kohli (74) to keep India firmly on course.

England vs India, third ODI, Lord’s England 387-3 after 50 overs (chose to bat): Ben Duckett (141 off 135), Jacob Bethell (91 off 93), Joe Root (74 off 48), Jos Buttler (41 off 13); Prasidh Krishna (2-69), Prince Yadav (1-79) India 260-7 after 50 overs: Rohit Sharma (138 off 110), Shubman Gill (77 off 84), Virat Kohli (74 off 60); Sam Curran (4-75), Jacob Bethell (1-49), Jofra Archer (1-63) Adil Rashid (1-64)

India were 303-2 and needed 84 from the final 39 balls when a decisive seven-ball spell saw Curran (4-75) dismiss Ishan Kishan (14), Shreyas Iyer (0) and Kohli, halting India's momentum as their chase fell 27 runs short.

After losing the series opener by six wickets at Edgbaston, England bounced back to secure a 2-1 ODI series victory over the world's top-ranked side, adding it to their 4-0 T20 series whitewash of India.

England clinch ODI series victory over India

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ben Duckett puts on a dominant display against India as he bats an amazing 141

Harry Brook completed a clean sweep of successful tosses with his third of the series, and his decision to bat paid immediate dividends as England's openers feasted on an Indian attack left rudderless without injured pace talisman Jasprit Bumrah.

India were made to toil in the field as England recorded a record 192-run first-wicket stand before Bethell picked out Rohit Sharma at cow corner to fall nine runs short of an emotional century on the day Lord's remembered Sir Garfield Sobers.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jacob Bethell is dismissed for 90 as he bats a superb innings in England's third ODI match against India

Duckett kicked on after reaching his century, blasting 18 fours and a six to surpass Sir Viv Richards' 138 not out against England in 1979 and register a new highest individual score in a Lord's ODI before falling caught and bowled to Prince Yadav.

Sports.title: 'I reached rock bottom' - Antonelli admits shock as title charge accelerates
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli has admitted he could not have imagined being in a dominant position at the top of the Formula 1 world championship 12 months ago when he reached "rock bottom" during his rookie campaign.

Antonelli, 19, won the Belgian Grand Prix for Mercedes on Sunday to move 45 points clear of Lewis Hamilton at the top of the drivers' standings, with 10 of 22 currently scheduled rounds complete.

Having been fast-tracked in by Mercedes boss Toto Wolff to replace Hamilton following the seven-time world champion's decision to join Ferrari, Antonelli endured a chastening spell midway through his 2025 campaign.

The then 18-year-old went on a dismal run during which he finished above ninth just once in 10 grands prix, with one of the low points coming as he was knocked out in Q1 in Belgium last year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli discusses his Belgian GP win and admits he's in a 'good position' after opening up a 45-point gap in the drivers' standings

Asked after claiming his sixth victory of the season on Sunday whether he could have imagined this scenario a year ago, Antonelli replied: "No, absolutely not.

"Last year here, I probably reached the bottom, so it was a very difficult weekend for me mentally.

"But this year was definitely a lot better. If you had asked me last year at this moment, I probably would have said no."

Antonelli's advantage at the top of the standings could actually be far greater if it were not for a spell of bad luck the Italian has endured in recent weeks.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli wins the Belgian Grand Prix

He suffered an engine failure when running second to Hamilton in Barcelona, and then suffered a wheel-guard failure that dropped him out of the points at the British Grand Prix when he appeared to be on course to chase Charles Leclerc down for victory.

His pace dominance over his team-mate George Russell, who began the year as the clear title favourite, makes it hard to see how Antonelli can be caught unless Ferrari make major improvements to their inferior power unit in the near future.

Despite his strong position, Antonelli is not dwelling on the increasing likelihood of him becoming by far the youngest driver to become an F1 world champion.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli joins Sky Sports' Karun Chandhok at the SkyPad to analyse the Italian's pole-setting lap at the Belgian Grand Prix

"I never want to relax too much," Antonelli told Sky Sports F1.

"Of course, it's a great result and good redemption after last year because last year was a very dark moment for me and to get the win is very special.

"But you can never relax because we have seen in the past how the situation can swing so quickly.

"So that's why it's important to really maximise and take every opportunity that is given, and just make the best out of it because you never know what can happen."

Wolff: We're all surprised by Antonelli form

Wolff made the decision to give Antonelli one of the most desirable seats on the grid when several other strong options were available, and there were times during 2025 when the choice came under great scrutiny.

While Wolff says Antonelli's ups and downs during his debut campaign were expected, the Austrian admits the teenager's remarkable consistency in 2026 has "surprised" the whole team.

"We're all surprised", Wolff said. "I think the first season came as expected. Great moments where his talent shined through, and then moments which were very difficult - the long spell of lack of results in the middle of the season, as expected.

"And then after the winter, also as expected, he knew the environment, he knew the pressures, he knew the demands of the team on the technical side, on the marketing side, knowing the tracks that we would go racing.

"But what was not expected is the serenity and structure that he brought into his game. With Kimi, whether the session was good or bad, you wouldn't see a difference in emotions in the debrief.

"It is absolutely transactional. What is the problem? How do we solve it? How do we move on? And that is new. And I think that's why it's almost when he wins, you can't see this absolute excitement that a 19-year-old would almost have."

Wolff highlighted Antonelli's reactions to the reliability issues that cost him in Barcelona and at Silverstone as further examples of his protégé's level-headedness.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli suffers damage during the British Grand Prix

Wolff added: "And at the same time, when he fails to deliver results, in Barcelona, when we had the car stoppage, or even in Silverstone, he comes back in and he was the one saying to the team, 'this is a mechanical sport, these things can happen'.

"Nineteen-years-old - that is very impressive to see. And I think this mindset and this attitude is probably one of the main drivers that has allowed the talent to shine so early in his career."

Sports.title: DeChambeau 'not a cheater' - Scheffler defends Bryson over rules drama
Sports.content:
Scottie Scheffler has defended Bryson DeChambeau over his rules controversy at The Open and has insisted the two-time US Open champion is ‘not a cheater’.

DeChambeau dominated headlines at Royal Birkdale during the final men's major of the year, where he appeared to be within a shot of the halfway lead before being handed a two-shot penalty after his second round.

The LIV Golf League star was adjudged to have improved the line of his backswing in long grass at the par-four fifth, turning his bogey into a triple-bogey seven, with DeChambeau involved in heated discussions with rules officials late into Friday evening.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sir Nick Faldo and Paul McGinley analysed Bryson DeChambeau's controversial two-stroke penalty from Friday and agreed he has not respected the rules of golf

Speculation that DeChambeau was set to withdraw in protest was quickly quashed by the American, who declined to speak to the media after every tournament round but said on social media that the decision 'fired him up' to continue.

Rory McIlroy criticised DeChambeau's "performative" behaviour, which included a lengthy discussion post-round on the course and a late-night range session, although the R&A accepted that his actions were unintentional.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy spoke to the media after his third round of The Open and said he was not impressed with Bryson DeChambeau's actions

"I've known him [DeChambeau] for a long time and he's a lot of things, but he's definitely not a cheater," Scheffler told reporters after his tied-fourth finish. "I've never seen him cheat once.

"Whether we were having a putting contest on the putting green or chipping contest, or anytime we played amateur golf, I never saw anything suspicious.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bryson DeChambeau was given a two-shot penalty after inadvertently improving his lie in thick rough on the fifth hole

"When you're watching him there from that camera angle, maybe he was a touch careless around his ball, but I don't think he did anything intentionally."

Scheffler held off talking about the incident after this third round but gave his views on the final day, with the world No 1 questioning whether there are different ways to enforce the rules.

"I think maybe we need to be a little bit more strict in the way that we are policing guys," Scheffler explained. "It's a little bit of a balance because you've got certain guys like Bryson, who every shot he hits is going to be shown on TV.

"When you have camera angles that are far away, things can look different than they do when you're right there. I feel like at times, sometimes you see players maybe push it a little bit further than they should.

"I think we need to get back to the traditions of the game and maybe we do need to police things a little bit more stricter in the game."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sam Burns said that 'there was not enough evidence' to penalise Bryson DeChambeau during the second round

Scheffler on near-miss: 'It wasn't my week'

Scheffler was aiming to become the first back-to-back winner of The Open since Padraig Harrington and briefly found himself within one of the lead on the final day, only to bogey the last and finish three strokes behind Ryan Fox.

"Today was a great effort," Scheffler insisted. "I felt like I was doing the right things out there. I gave myself a lot of looks again today. I guess it just wasn't my week.

"I got a good break there on 17, but off the tee, it probably should have been in the fairway. That stuff hurts. My ball on 13 goes into that hole. It wasn't my best tee shot, but it was a time where I needed to be aggressive.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Scottie Scheffler raged after his tee shot found the rough on the par-five 17th hole at Royal Birkdale

"I saw some good stuff happening with guys that hit the ball over there the last few days, and it didn't happen for me today. Just those little bounces. My ball on 14 I think is in the fairway, I come up there, it's in the pot bunker. Little stuff like that over the course of the week tends to add up.

"I competed really well this week. I did a good job of staying patient and hit the ball really nice over the course of four days. Maybe yesterday was the only day I didn't strike it as well as I would have liked to."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the final round of The Open, where Ryan Fox claimed an impressive maiden major victory

Sports.title: World Cup final: Trump, half-time show and everything but the football – live
Sports.content:
4m ago 15.47 EDT Does the World Cup final need a halftime show? The argument for the halftime show seems to be that it’s what new fans want. James Massing of Live Nation, who are helping put on the show, told the BBC that sports events need to change things up because they are “competing with any other live experience - going to the museum, going to the theatre, going to the cinema”. I’m pretty sure no one going to the museum expects a halftime show though, and people are still happy to queue up to see the Mona Lisa without one. I suspect that this is also a push by people who think that US fans will refuse to watch a big event unless it has a halftime show, even though plenty of big sporting events, from the NBA finals to the World Series don’t have halftime shows. I actually think the appeal of soccer to many Americans is that it’s not the NFL, in the same way that many European fans enjoy the NFL because it’s not soccer. And people expect a halftime show at the Super Bowl because it’s the Super Bowl, not because they expect - or want - one at a World Cup final. Added to that, the best Super Bowl halftime shows often provide commentary on the state of America, from Bad Bunny’s hymn to immigrants at this year’s Super Bowl to Beyonce’s black panther tribute in 2016. Somehow, I doubt Gianni and friends are going to allow Shakira to sneak in references to the Iran War today. On the upside, all the artists are performing for free, there will be a kids choir and the show is meant to support Fifa’s education fund. Share

21m ago 15.30 EDT Sam Jones Madrid’s Plaza de Colón, famous for its massive Spanish flag, is absolutely rammed as the match begins. Police are turning people away from the barriers that have been installed around the square, but the mood inside it somewhere between expectant and buoyant. No one wants to hex the game but hopes are high.



“It’s a historic moment and it’s really exciting,” said Katy, 18, who was two years old the last time Spain won the World Cup. “I’m obviously hoping that Spain win and I think it’ll be 3-2 to Spain.” Miguel Hinojal Vicente, 37, had come to Madrid from Toledo as much for the party atmosphere as for the match itself. Unlike Katy, he had vivid memories of Spain’s last World Cup triumph. “Shit, it was just a magical thing,” he said. “But, to tell the truth, I’m more of a Atleti fan than a Spain fan.” His friend Raquel Garcia was a little more enthusiastic - and optimistic. She predicted a 3-0 win for Spain, with two goals in the first half and one in the second. But it was about more than just football for her. “This is about the hopes of a country and it’s about unity,” she said. “Events like these bring people together and they make people happy.” Share

I’m going with the 27th minute, after he’s exhausted himself rage-bleating on Truth Social during the first commercial break about the large number of “probably illegal” Latinos in the stadium. Here’s a little more on the subject in our video explainer: Scandal-proof: why Infantino's Fifa power can't be touched – video Share

1h ago 14.22 EDT An organization called The Final Red Card is arranging a protest around today’s final. According to the organization: “During today’s Fifa World Cup Final, thousands of fans are expected to raise commemorative referee-style red cards in a coordinated, peaceful visual action during the tournament’s trophy presentation, transforming soccer’s most universally recognized symbol into a global call for democracy, accountability, and a repudiation of Trump’s corruption. “The action, titled The Final Red Card, is being organized by a coalition of artists, organizers, and advocacy organizations led by SoundsGood, the campaign activation studio behind the nationally covered Flags in the Stands: ICE OUT activation during Super Bowl LX, together with Contra-ICE, Make the Road New Jersey, 50501, People vs. The Machine, South Asians for America, Way to Win, Movement Voter Project, and additional national and local partners.” Share

2h ago 14.18 EDT Alexander Abnos Marine One has just flown over the stadium with two escort helicopters Share

2h ago 14.14 EDT Weather watch The New York area has been swamped by smoke from Canadian wildfires for much of the last few days but, after storms last night, the air is clear (by local standards). Temperatures will be around 82F/28C at kickoff, nowhere near as sweltering as we saw for France v Paraguay or England v Norway, so it’s unlikely conditions will affect the players – particularly as Spanish and Argentinians players will be used to playing in the heat. Share

2h ago 14.06 EDT Alexander Abnos The White House press pool has arrived at the stadium, which caused the temporary closure of every ramp and staircase on the north side of the stadium. The president is presumably quite close by. Share

2h ago 13.59 EDT Streamer IShowSpeed, probably more famous than 98% of the players at this World Cup, is performing too. It’s probably not even watching the match now that he’s been on. View image in fullscreen IShowSpeed performs during the closing ceremony. Photograph: Héctor Vivas/FIFA/Getty Images Share

2h ago 13.56 EDT Post Malone has rocked up to perform at the closing ceremony, which is now taking place. Swae Lee joins him for toe tapper Sunflower. View image in fullscreen Post Malone and Swae Lee perform during the closing ceremony. Photograph: Alex Pantling/FIFA/Getty Images Share

2h ago 13.53 EDT Just a reminder that the halftime show will last 25 to 30 minutes. Around 11 minutes for the actual show and the rest of the time to set up the stage and then take it all down. There are worries that the added down time for players could lead to injuries as muscles cool down due to inactivity. On the upside, they’ll get to hear Justin Bieber sing for about 90 seconds. The list of artists includes: Shakira; Burna Boy; BTS; Madonna; Kermit and Miss Piggy; conductor Gustavo Dudamel with musicians from the New York Philharmonic and the Simon Bolivar Symphony Orchestra of Venezuela; dance troupe Ghetto Kids; Emmanuel Kelly; PS 22 Chorus (cute kids from a local school). Share Updated at 14.33 EDT

2h ago 13.46 EDT Facundo Iglesia is on the ground for us in Buenos Aires to take in the atmosphere among Argentina fans: Argentines can’t be accused of tempering their trademark intensity – or their superstitions – in the hours leading up to the World Cup final. On the eve of the match, thousands of people - mostly parents with their children – flocked to Buenos Aires’ Parque Rivadavia to trade or buy Panini stickers, racing to fill their albums just in time. Many tucked stickers of the Spanish players into freezers, an accessible, popularized bit of witchcraft meant to curse the opposing squad. Now, on the day of the final, under a persistent drizzle, hundreds are waving flags and blowing vuvuzelas at the Obelisco - the city’s designated meeting point to celebrate the national team, whatever the result may be. The streets leading to the monument are packed with fans and street vendors hawking flags, face paint, and plastic ponchos. María de las Nieves López, a Paraguayan pizzeria owner who traveled from Ezeiza, a city 35 kilometers outside the capital, wasn’t fazed by the rain or the lack of a screen near the monument. “It’s Lio [Messi]’s last one. We wanted to come and cheer him and the rest of the squad on - to support them from here. We’ll watch the game on our phones if we have to,” she said. López, who has lived in the country for 25 years, carried a 20-year-old doll she credits with bringing “good luck,” because it “had watched all the games.” “Well, we’ve been winning so far,” she said. “I promised her that, if Argentina wins the final, I’ll buy her a new dress.” Share

2h ago 13.41 EDT The closing ceremony is off to a good start. Or rather not start at all. It was supposed to get underway 90 mins before kickoff but is yet to do so. There are often delays when Donald Trump attends sporting events as the arena is secured. It’s unclear as yet whether kickoff will be delayed. I’m sure they can scrap some bits of this closing ceremony to hurry things along. No one will mind if Robbie Williams is bumped, surely? Share

2h ago 13.38 EDT Alexander Abnos is at the stadium for us, and has some team news (sort of): Spain have just entered the stadium and are wandering around in the center of the field. A team of Fifa volunteers are gathered holding what looks to be a very large tarp, which presumably will be a key part of the closing ceremony. I think Spain team may have to move.... View image in fullscreen The world’s most famous tarp in action. Photograph: Elsa/Getty Images And here comes the tarp! It’s an artistic and frankly kinda tacky composite of a number of New York City landmarks. Clockwise from bottom left on your TV screens: The new Calatrava train hub at World Trade Center, 1 World Trade, The Brooklyn Bridge, the Empire State Building, The Vessel, some building I don’t recognize, the Guggenheim, the Chrysler Building, the Statue of Liberty, 30 Rock, the Washington Square arch, the Flatiron building. Share Updated at 13.43 EDT

2h ago 13.36 EDT Good news from Fifa! There will be a “fan-centric pre-match ceremony” today, which means “an immersive, 360-degree concept that transforms the stadium into a shared stage. No matter where supporters are seated, each will have a distinct and engaging perspective, with extra-large country flag banners and on-pitch elements carefully positioned to involve the crowd in an authentic and meaningful way.” I bet there’s a hologram. There is always a hologram. It gets better though. At long last, Fifa is going to pay attention to its poor, neglected sponsors: “the youth programme and players’ tunnel will feature both traditional and new integrations of FIFA’s Commercial Partners, thanks to the involvement of adidas, Coca-Cola, Kia, Mengniu, Qatar Airways and Quaker.” At first, I read that as “quakers” and I was expecting a silent prayer meeting, which would have been quite nice. The pre-match ceremony will also include “additional elements such as coloured smoke or pyrotechnics.” Coloured smoke OR pyrotechnics? $5,000 a ticket and you don’t even get both? This better be a good game. Share

Sports.title: Kane says Tuchel will ‘learn a lot’ from England pressures after exit to Argentina
Sports.content:
Harry Kane has backed Thomas Tuchel to learn from England’s World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina and believes they must use the forthcoming Nations League campaign to gain experience of playing against the top teams.

Kane was an unused substitute as England sealed third place with an entertaining 6-4 victory against France on Saturday – their best finish at a World Cup on foreign soil. Tuchel, who signed a contract extension before the tournament, has been criticised heavily for his tactics against Argentina when he opted to switch to a back five to try to defend a 1-0 lead.

Kane admitted England had fallen short against Lionel Scaloni’s side but described the environment Tuchel has created since succeeding Gareth Southgate in 2025 as “the best England group I’ve been a part of in terms of togetherness”.

The captain said: “I know there are a lot of questions after the other night. We have to process it as players. I’m sure the manager will. It’s his first major tournament. He’ll learn a lot from the players, the situations, the pressures, the travel.

“There are also a lot of things as players we can learn from the other night. For now it’s just trying to process everything. We had a lot of good things, a lot of tough situations we overcame. The group is incredible, the best England group I’ve been a part of in terms of togetherness. The boss was a big part of creating that as well.

“Fans are going to be angry and we understand it. It’s a major tournament and that’s why you dream so big. When it doesn’t go your way you have to take the criticism. We’re all willing to do that, to dare to reach the biggest goal of all. We know over the next two years until we’re facing that situation again there is always going to be a question mark. It’s something we have to take and use as motivation.”

England missed out on facing regular top-class opposition in the buildup to the World Cup after being relegated from the top Nations League group in 2022 under Southgate. They were promoted in 2024 and will face Spain, Croatia and Czechia, starting with a rematch of the Euro 2024 final against Luis de la Fuente’s side on 26 September at Wembley. After beating France – albeit in a largely meaningless game – Kane thinks England must take the competition seriously if they are to thrive in tournaments.

View image in fullscreen Defeat to an established opponent was a familiar feeling for England. Photograph: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images

“The last 30 minutes of Argentina is not the team we want to be,” he said. “We spent a lot of time over the last two years talking about that situation, to attack those moments. The bottom line is we lost anyway. It’s easy to go away and talk about it. We need to get better at actually being in those situations. We can train, play the qualifiers … I think the Nations League will be big for us, against Spain and Croatia, big teams.

“Getting used to those big environments and finding our best form against those teams, like we did against France, albeit not in the most competitive match. We have to learn, improve. The coach will have improved from these learnings. I can talk as much as I want but ultimately it’s about showing it next time we’re in that situation.”
