Kane has been on the losing side in two World Cup semi-finals and two European Championship finals and he believes Tuchel is the man to help England to make the final step.

“The enthusiasm he has, the emotion he brings, the tactical experience he has … it doesn’t mean you’re going to get it right every time. We want to get it right on the biggest occasions and he expects that from himself as well. He’s a fantastic coach. He not only gave the players belief but he gave the country belief that it was our year. That is why it hurts even more than other years because everyone believed we were going all the way.

“Everyone has to process it. He has to process it himself. We’re still in that grieving stage, the emotional stage, and we’ll be in that for the next few weeks. It won’t be until the next camp where you think about what the future holds and what the next target is. We’ll have conversations as captain and manager and with other teammates and staff, to see where we can be better.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Give it up for Vozinha, Spence and the 2026 World Cup’s cult heroes
Sports.content:
WE CAN BE HEROES

Every World Cup produces cult heroes, icons who make it possible for us to sit back and start misty-eyed recollections by saying: “Do you remember Roger Milla/Saeed Al-Owairan/Keisuke Honda/Paul the Octopus?” Well, the Geopolitics World Cup has not let us down! Here are 10 cult heroes who’ve emerged from this tournament.

Yaya Sithole: a catastrophic start as the South Africa midfielder’s error led to the first goal of the GWC against Mexico, compounded by a second-half red card. Bounced back with a vital display in the win over South Korea, leading his country to the knockout round. Decades from now, people will still be talking about the Yaya Sithole redemption arc. Possibly.

Vozinha: who else? Cape Verde’s players all became cult heroes, but especially the 40-year-old keeper who spent last season in the Portuguese second tier and this summer keeping out Spain as the Blue Sharks went unbeaten in the group stage, then pushed Argentina to extra time in the last 32. Vozinha’s mum: get in line – we’re all in his fan club now.

Djed Spence: a toss-up with Dan “the modern-day header-beast” Burn for England’s cult hero, but let’s give it to the Spurs full-back who transformed from the hapless scourge of Thomas Tuchel’s existence in the group stage to a chin-strapped Cafu in the knockout round. Spence’s slide tackle on Giuliano Simeone (albeit sans chin-strap) will live long in the memory.

View image in fullscreen Djed Spence to the rescue. Photograph: Will Oliver/EPA

Matías Galarza: Paraguay’s most magnificent git was always involved despite rarely trying to play football. Almost every time we saw the midfielder he was moaning, playacting, needling opponents – truly putting the “art” into the dark arts. Also scored against Turkey and later nicked the referee’s watch and strapped it to his own wrist. Timeless ’housery.

Keyne: poor Lamine Yamal, who turned a craggy 19 during the GWC, must be feeling pretty aged considering he’s been usurped by his three-year-old brother. Keyne gurning and giggling in the crowd has delighted fans in Spain and beyond. Considering some of the other people who’ve hogged TV cutaways, the toddler has been a welcome sight.

Iván Barton: Salvadorian referee grabbed the globe’s attention when he sent off Miguel Almirón, bawling at the winger like a mum sending a misbehaving youngster to bed with no dinner. “After review, No 10, Paraguay, covered his mouth! The decision is red card!” No PlayStation either, Miguel!

Eloy Room: move over, Vozinha, and make room for Eloy! Yep, another veteran goalie starred at this GWC as Curaçao bounced back from shipping seven (7) against Germany to hold Ecuador to a 0-0 draw. The 37-year-old Room made 15 saves – a record for a 90-minute World Cup match – to earn the tiny Caribbean island their first ever point.

View image in fullscreen Eloy Room to the rescue. Photograph: Ed Zurga/AP

Danny Murphy: or should it be Bob the cat? The deadpan BBC pundit’s tale of how a family moggy once made a break for freedom inside a Royal Mail van – sparked by Oscar Bobb coming off the bench for Norway – proved so engrossing that viewers demanded, and got, several follow-ups. A purr-fect hydration-break diversion. Honk!

Hossam Hassan: Egypt’s perma-angry, black T-shirted head coach was an intimidating presence – especially paired with his identical twin brother, the team director, Ibrahim Hassan. The pair had a row with Dallas police, led the Pharaohs to the last 16, saw Egypt take a 2-0 lead against Argentina … before the final 15 minutes helped Hossam reach new heights of apoplexy.

Romelu Lukaku: how can Belgium’s record goalscorer be obscure enough for cult-hero status? Well, when you polish off USA USA USA 4-1 and celebrate your 93rd international goal with a Trump dance near the corner flag in the aftermath of Balogungate. Thanks, Big Rom (Bigliest Rom?) – the planet is with you.

View image in fullscreen Romelu Lukaku to the rescue. Photograph: Lindsey Wasson/AP

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Rob Smyth from 8pm BST (3pm EST, 5am AEST) for hot updates from Spain 1-1 Argentina (aet; 4-5 on pens) in the GWC final. The animals below agree, though the punters in New York City disagree. Meanwhile Tom Lutz will be in situ for another liveblog mopping up all other business outside the game, which we’re tempted to call Everything But The Goal.

View image in fullscreen Moo Deng, a two-year-old female pygmy hippopotamus, picks Argentina at Khao Kheow Open Zoo in Thailand Photograph: Anusak Laowilas/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

View image in fullscreen Poty the jaguar sides with the holders too at BioParque, in Rio de Janeiro. Photograph: Tita Barros/Reuters

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“This game will help us for sure – even if you can never fully celebrate a bronze medal. It’s the first [men’s World Cup] medal for 60 years, first [at a men’s] World Cup on foreign soil, and I hope the players can be proud of that at some point. We set ourselves the highest dream to chase, and we were very, very ambitious with our dream to make the final in the World Cup. So it’s very, very painful if you miss out, the pain will stay for a while” – England head coach Thomas Tuchel after overseeing a quite preposterous 6-4 win over France in the Third Place Play-off.

View image in fullscreen England with their bronzes. Photograph: Paul Childs/Reuters

double quotation mark May I be one of the 1,057 pedants to point out that it’s little wonder Brazil lost to Poland in the 1970 TPPO (yesterday’s Football Daily) as they would have been resting players for the next day’s final against Italy (which they won 4-1 to claim their third world crown – Pelé, Carlos Alberto and all that). You must have meant the 1974 TPPO. Easy to be fatigued at this stage of the tournament; just ask Harry Kane” – Jonathan Westwood (and 1,056 others).

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Jonathan Westwood (and the 1,056 others). Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

Sports.title: Fifa gives fraud ‘an open door’ with betting, says Council of Europe chief
Sports.content:
Fifa has been accused of providing an “open door to fraud” and allowing political influence to cast doubt on the integrity of the World Cup in a stinging rebuke by the Council of Europe’s secretary general.

In an open letter published to coincide with Sunday’s final, Alain Berset also called for a new integrity framework to be built before the 2030 tournament, which is mainly being staged in Europe, and warned that Fifa was embroiled in a crisis involving money and power.

Berset referenced the scandal surrounding Fifa’s decision to shelve the suspension of the USA striker Folarin Balogun and made apparent allusions to comments made by the Paraguayan senator Celeste Amarilla about Kylian Mbappé and by the former Spanish prime minister Mariano Rajoy about the France team.

“The Fifa World Cup 2026 has raised question after question,” Berset wrote. “A sanction suspended under pressure, within days, with no reasons given. The authority of referees called into question. Racist abuse of players, some of it from elected officials. Betting on every pass, every card, every corner. The celebration will end tonight. The questions will not.”

It is a significant intervention given Fifa and the Council of Europe signed a memorandum of understanding in 2018, which remains valid. The agreement was struck to strengthen their work together on a number of topics, including “human rights, integrity and good governance in sport”. Open criticism of one partner by another is extremely rare.

Berset took aim at Fifa’s deal with ADI Predictstreet, which became the World Cup’s official prediction market partner in April. “Betting has moved from the result of a match to moments a single player can produce without changing the score,” he said. “A bet is won by making others lose. It is an open door to fraud. And this World Cup has opened the door wider.”

In further reference to the lifting of Balogun’s ban by Fifa, which occurred after a phone call to its president, Gianni Infantino, by his US counterpart, Donald Trump, Berset said: “When the rules bend under pressure, every result is open to doubt.”

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino with Donald Trump at the World Cup final reception at Trump Tower on Friday 17 July in New York. Photograph: Ira L Black/Fifa/Getty Images

Infantino has said the decision to revoke Balogun’s ban was taken independently by Fifa’s disciplinary committee “based on the applicable regulations and the specific facts”.

Berset, who is Swiss, proposed a “working dialogue that starts tonight” to begin the “urgent work of strengthening the integrity of sport” before future World Cups. He referenced work by the Council of Europe – which is the continent’s intergovernmental human rights organisation – in creating a binding treaty to keep fans safe three months after the Heysel Stadium disaster in 1985, as well as further legislation set up to tackle doping in athletics and match-fixing.

The letter comes a week and a half after 72 members of the European parliament wrote to the 27 EU-based football associations asking for an investigation into Infantino’s involvement in the Balogun case. It pointed to alleged breaches of political neutrality and suggested Fifa had contravened its own code of ethics.

It does not appear likely that Uefa, European football’s governing body, will formally take the matter further. In June, 50 members of the European parliament wrote to Infantino and the Fifa council requesting an investigation into the awarding of the Fifa peace prize to Trump.

Fifa was contacted for comment.

This past week it was revealed that more that 200 of Fifa’s member associations have formally backed Infantino’s attempt to be re-elected for a fourth term in March.

Sports.title: England 2026 World Cup squad: player-by-player ratings
Sports.content:
Goalkeepers

Jordan Pickford Could he have done better with Enzo Fernández’s equaliser for Argentina? Jude Bellingham certainly thought so. But the man who has made more World Cup finals appearances than any other Englishman made some crucial saves, including a brilliant stop from Nicolas González in the semi-final. 7

Dean Henderson Had to wait until the third-place playoff for some action and ended up conceding four goals despite a strong performance. Will hope to challenge Pickford over next two years. 7

Defenders

Djed Spence Emerged as an unlikely cult hero thanks to some wholehearted performances. He will always be remembered for snubbing Thomas Partey’s handshake and his tackle on Giuliano Simeone against Argentina. 8

Marc Guéhi Somehow wasn’t Thomas Tuchel’s first-choice initially, although that was rectified after the Croatia game. England’s most consistent and reliable defender – the way he handled Erling Haaland was a masterclass. 8

John Stones Arrived painfully short of match fitness and it showed in the opening game against Croatia. Much improved when called upon in the quarter- and semi-finals. A huge asset when he plays. 7

Ezri Konsa A few shaky moments during the group stage but recovered well and filled in capably at right-back when needed. At 28, young enough to be there again in four years. 7

View image in fullscreen Dan Burn’s headed block from this Raúl Jiménez bicycle kick cleared the halfway line. Photograph: Ulises Ruiz/AFP/Getty Images

Dan Burn Showed his limitations against Argentina. But he will always have those two epic appearances off the bench against Mexico and Norway. No one will forget the clearing headers so powerful they ended up in the opposition’s half. 7

Nico O’Reilly Had his strongest game against Norway in the quarter-final when he was at his marauding best. Will be disappointed not to have scored and to have been on the pitch as a substitute when Argentina instigated their semi-final comeback. 6

Reece James Such a good player when fit, which is sadly far too rare. Missed most of the tournament owing to a hamstring injury and England suffered when he went off against Argentina. 6

Trevoh Chalobah The Chelsea player was a surprise choice to replace Tino Livramento, who pulled out injured at the last minute. Managed only six minutes against France in the end. 6

Jarell Quansah Brought in to solve the right-back conundrum against Panama, he was doing well until the rush of blood against Mexico and subsequent red card. Recalled for the France game and had to be replaced. 5

Midfielders

Jude Bellingham Showed his supreme quality when it mattered and could not be more committed to his country’s cause, even if his rocky relationship with Tuchel had to be carefully managed. 9

Elliot Anderson Didn’t allow himself to be distracted by his £116m move to Manchester City and grew as the tournament progressed. Ran his heart out against Norway and Argentina. 8

View image in fullscreen Morgan Rogers (left) crossed for Anthony Gordon to put England ahead against Argentina. Photograph: Julian Finney/FIFA/Getty Images

Morgan Rogers Made the most of his limited minutes in unfamiliar roles. Showed what a good player he is by playing as one of the two central midfielders against Norway before setting up Anthony Gordon from the right wing against Argentina. 8

Declan Rice Clearly affected by the hamstring and back problems that marred the second half of his season with Arsenal, even if his effort – as ever – could not be faulted. Needs a long rest to recharge his batteries but may not get one. 6

Eberechi Eze Could not have the impact he would have wished for in four substitute appearances before starting against France. Did a decent job in central midfield against Panama but was largely on the periphery when given a chance on the left in the quarter-final. 6

Jordan Henderson Spent 12 minutes on the pitch, in a historic appearance against Panama when he became the first England men’s player to appear at seven major international tournaments. But managed to get booked against Mexico as a substitute and break an arm celebrating the win. 5

Forwards

Bukayo Saka Three goals and three assists despite playing through the pain of an achilles injury was a courageous effort from Arsenal’s talisman. It was a huge surprise not to see him come off the bench against Argentina and he showed what England were missing against France. 8

Anthony Gordon A quiet start having been preferred to Rashford before responding magnificently to being dropped. Three assists and a goal against Argentina showed why Barcelona were so keen to sign him. 8

View image in fullscreen Harry Kane’s two goals against the Democratic Republic of the Congo saved England from an early exit. Photograph: Cristóbal Herrera/EPA

Harry Kane Sadly his tournament will be remembered for a largely anonymous display against Argentina rather than rescuing England against the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Will he ever have a better chance to win the World Cup? 8

Marcus Rashford Made a good start to his third World Cup by coming off the bench to score against Croatia, and started against Panama. But wasn’t seen again until England were chasing the game against Argentina in injury time. 6

Ivan Toney Sat on the bench until Lautaro Martínez’s goal in added time of the semi-final. Could not make an impact in the three minutes he was given but did well against France. 6

Ollie Watkins Largely a frustrated spectator despite his heroics in the Euro 2024 semi-final and arriving here in a rich vein of form. A half on the left flank against France and a brief appearance against Panama were scant reward. 6

Noni Madueke Some promising moments but lacked end product in his four starts and had slipped down the pecking order by the semi-final. Needs to be much more clinical at this level. 5

Did not play: James Trafford and Kobbie Mainoo

Sports.title: Fifa to announce record $15bn World Cup revenue, smashing expectations
Sports.content:
Fifa will announce record $15bn (£11.2bn) revenues from this summer’s World Cup, significantly exceeding the targets set before the tournament.

Fifa’s member associations were informed of the boost in income by Gianni Infantino on Saturday. Originally the governing body had projected $11bn in earnings. Sources have indicated that hospitality and ticketing, especially through the steeply priced secondary market, account for a significant amount of the increase. Fifa takes 15% from the buyer and another 15% from the seller on the secondary market.

It is likely that football associations will reap the benefits of Fifa’s expanded World Cup pot, although details are yet to be finalised. The financial situation will come as a boost to Infantino, who will feel it further shores up his position after a controversy-ridden month in the US, Canada and Mexico.

There was widespread fury after Fifa was perceived to have bowed to pressure from Donald Trump in suspending the red card given to Folarin Balogun, the US striker, against Bosnia and Herzegovina in the last 32. Fifa has said the decision was taken independently by its disciplinary committee but that has continued to fester among European FAs in particular. Infantino has nevertheless received more than 200 pledges of support from Fifa’s member associations for his re-election in March. The prospect of extra funds from bumper World Cup revenue is likely to dissuade some FAs from making any discontent public.

Such a bonanza may also increase the chances of the US hosting another edition in the near future. The next World Cup available for bids is the 2038 tournament. At a reception on Friday, Trump confirmed his country’s eagerness for a repeat performance. “You should choose the United States of America again,” he said. “This time we will leave Canada and Mexico out.” The US has also held talks with Fifa about hosting the Club World Cup in 2029.

On Saturday evening, VIP and hospitality packages for Sunday’s final between Spain and Argentina, which was played in New Jersey, were still listed on Fifa’s ticketing portal. Tickets for the “trophy lounge” were retailing at $34,500 per person.

Sports.title: America’s World Cup report card: some As for atmosphere, but F for affordability
Sports.content:
Come rain or smokescreen, Sunday will bring the 2026 World Cup to its bombastic end. The load-bearer of the co-hosting North American trio, the United States held 78 of the tournament’s matches across its 11 host cities. Only two contests remain: the third-place game in Miami, and the big one in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

Before the dust truly settles and focus shifts to the six-nation, three-continent centennial in 2030, how did the United States fare in its second swing at hosting a men’s World Cup?

Stadiums

Depending on what you’re looking for, best in class. Few venues have “charm” in the traditional sense, but these sprawling NFL venues packed in plenty of fans, with many designed to retain sound to harness atmosphere. That said, none seem to have figured out how to adequately keep a concourse congregation flowing, with those corridors hardly expanded to account for so many people in one building. B+

Transport

This was an anticipated drawback of holding this tournament in the US, as the nation rebuilt itself throughout the 20th century with clear priorities for the automobile. Some cities stepped up their public transportation options with ad‑hoc buses; others used those initiatives to further eat into riders’ spending budgets. Hours spent slowly progressing to venues, and even more slowly when leaving, were equally costly. D+

Affordability

Do we even need to explain this one? The expectations for ticket pricing made public in United 26’s bid book were in line with what we’ve come to expect for World Cups, with inflation largely justifying modest increases from tournament to tournament. Instead, the 2026 World Cup became an outlier for event pricing of nearly any kind – the first that most of the world could never afford to attend.

Fifa admitted this was a rare chance to spawn an ATM from the tournament’s rib, and that the ludicrously priced inventory wouldn’t be sustainable for future installments on other continents. An unapologetic slap in the face of USsoccer fans. Once Fifa set this precedent, every other stakeholder in the tournament – transport, food and beverage vendors, merchandisers, parking lot operators, taxis, everyone – followed suit. F

View image in fullscreen Even if you had a ticket to a World Cup match in Philadelphia, the price of parking was no small feat. Photograph: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images

Hospitality

On the one hand, the displays of community were incredibly touching. No matter how overpriced the lager was, it was common to see traveling fans from all over the world clinking cups before and after the match. Fifa’s legion of volunteers were smiling faces in neon tracksuits, awfully helpful and welcoming at every turn.

On the other hand, not all fans were quite so well accommodated. Referees and team staffers were among those turned away by Trump administration decisions. That precedent also left the general fan from a Trump-banned nation without a chance of getting around policies. The rationale for those rejections was incredibly flimsy, yet Fifa stood beside the man in the White House.

It will be impossible not to wonder how different the support of Côte d’Ivoire, Haiti, Iran and Senegal could have been had the tourist accessibility of the 1994 World Cup been replicated. A for the spirit fostered by those who could make it, but F for the unprecedented barriers set before qualifiers and customers alike.

Atmosphere

The category with the biggest discrepancies between the best-in-class and the rest. Some – Seattle, Philadelphia and Kansas City – cemented an identity of being organic and sustainable soccer cities. The “World Cup village” atmosphere so many fans covet was alive and well, with accessible public watch parties, signage and flags lining streets, and a constant buzz of excitement that the world’s eyes found their neck of the woods. Others, like Boston – the second capital of Scotland – and the Bay Area either embraced their temporary occupants or had plenty of space and opportunities for locals to keep the party going between matchdays.

Others, especially those whose stadiums weren’t in or adjacent to the city center, really struggled to harness the tournament’s potential. It turns out being an hour or two away from the action feels just as invigorating to some as watching a game from their sofa. Texas seemed especially agnostic despite being one of two states with multiple host cities, with dispatches from Dallas and Houston reading equally blase. The roadshow has already packed up, and many in some of these cities will hardly recognize what came through. B-

Sports.title: Fans left baffled by Tom Cruise's pre-World Cup final 'Ted Talk' as Hollywood icon makes bizarre speech to rouse fans before kick-off
Sports.content:
Tom Cruise opened World Cup final blockbuster with an emotional monologue following a calamitous closing ceremony.

Defending champions Argentina bid to secure a second successive World Cup triumph in a showdown against Spain in front of 80,000 clamoring fans, including President Donald Trump, at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on Sunday.

Even before the first kick of the game, the spectators inside the stadium, as well as the billions watching from home, an eye-catching spectacle played out on the MetLife turf.

A bevy of Hollywood's finest had been billed as performers with Cruise headlining the event, designed to pay tribute to all of the competing 48 nations from the tournament.

However, fans anxious to see the Hollywood icon, 64, were made to wait for almost 90 minutes as they had to endure a bizarre performance from YouTuber IShowSpeed in the buildup to kickoff.

Cruise finally made his long-awaited appearance less than 10 minutes before the teams walked out onto the pitch. FIFA reserved the actor for the grand finale of the ceremony with Cruise reflecting on the tournament, which has been the biggest in World Cup history.

Tom Cruise opened World Cup final blockbuster with an emotional monologue

The Hollywood side headlined the closing ceremony ahead of the final at MetLife Stadium

Nicole Scherzinger, Robbie Williams and Laura Pausini also featured in the spectacle

'More than 30 days ago, 48 nations began a journey,' Cruise began. 'They crossed oceans. They crossed borders. They crossed cultures. And together they showed us why this game belongs to the world.'

He continued: 'From three countries across them, and from every corner of the globe, we have witnessed greatness, and we have shared in moments of joy, moments of hope, moments we will all never forget. Football is a language spoken without words, a force that unites people, that turns strangers into friends and reminds us of what we all have in common.

'So as we gather for one final chapter, let us celebrate a tournament that brought the world together. Let us celebrate each other. This is football. This is unity. This is greatness.'

Fans were left baffled by the address with one viewer writing on X: 'I'm disappointed Tom Cruise did not helicopter in for his Ted talk. FIFA missed an opportunity to collaborate with a chopper company.'

'About as inspiring as watching your cat get run over,' added another.

Others took issue with the message of unity with some pointing to the travel and visa chaos that some teams, including Iran, had to endure before and throughout the tournament due to US customs and border enforcement.

'Brought the world together. You banned Iran from entering your country until game day,' one fan claimed on X. 'And banned a referee from turning up.'

'That had nothing to do with football,' insisted another. 'Just more USA'in (sic) c**p. How did the USA treat the Iranian team and players? Disgracefully, as fittingly represents the USA.'

Popular streamer IShowSpeed kickstarted the World Cup final closing ceremony

The streamer surprised viewers when he began performing an original song, Champions

The Mission Impossible star has been spotted in the stands throughout the tournament and performed a stunt at the Paris Olympics' closing ceremony

Cruise had been billed as the main attraction, but fans were left confused to first see IShowSpeed dominating their screens rather than the legendary actor when the closing ceremony got underway.

The content creator - who has over 58 million subscribers on YouTube and streamed multiple matches throughout the World Cup - stunned fans by launching into song.

He had been listed as a performer but he surprised viewers when he began performing original song, Champions, which was on the official 2026 World Cup album.

The streamer began lying down to croon up into an overhead broadcast camera, before rising to his feet and showing off his moves amid a colorful array of backup dancers in neon tracksuits.

Post Malone replaced IShowSpeed in the spotlight. More accustomed to performing, he opened with his new track Chrome Heartbreaker, before leading into his 2018 song Wow for his three-song performance.

He then brought out rapper Swae Lee to perform their grammy-nominated hit Sunflower.

Post, 31, rocked a classic Canadian tuxedo, accessorizing with his signature cowboy hat and sunglasses.

The content creator performed at MetLife Stadium amid a neon swarm of dancers

Post Malone (right) performed his 2018 hit Sunflower with Swae Lee (left)

Scherzinger, Williams and Pausini performed the official FIFA anthem, Desire

IShowSpeed, who boasts over 58 million subscribers on YouTube, dressed in an all-white suit

The American singer and rapper pulled aside his denim jacket to unveil a t-shirt that read: 'I just hope both teams have fun.' The shirt's message was a nod to Elmo's now-viral tweet ahead of the NBA Finals that left New Yorkers furious.

However, fans were left underwhelmed at the bizarre opening display with many bemoaning the lack of creativity and star-power.

'Such an underwhelming closing ceremony. Zero creativity just artists singing,' one wrote on X.

'The lip syncing for these closing ceremony performances is horrific,' another shared.

'ishowspeed was so random,' said a third, while another baffled viewer branded it 'unreal scenes.'

'Imagine telling someone a few years ago that ishowspeed is gonna perform at the world cup,' added a fifth.

Another went on: 'Worst closing ceremony.. obviously low budget.'

'The World Cup closing show was terrible - lousy production, just like the opening ceremony,' said one X user.

Meanwhile, others questioned why a content creator was given the honor of performing on the world's biggest stage.

'Why should speed be at the world cup final singing in the first place???. At least his idol doesn't make final,' one fan argued.

Post, 31, rocked a classic Canadian tuxedo, accessorizing with his signature cowboy hat

Williams cut a particularly striking figure in a bedazzled electric blue tracksuit

Fans were left underwhelmed at the bizarre display, slamming the 'random' performances

'I don't know what's going on or who this is or why we thought we should have this represent us to the rest of the world,' another added.

'I legitimately have never heard of this person,' said a third.

Oscar winner Jennifer Hudson was granted the honor of performing the US national anthem. The singer, dressed in an elegant Thom Browne skirt suit, wowed fans with her powerful rendition of The Star-Spangled Banner.

Ahead of Cruise's speech, British singer Robbie Williams was joined by Tony winner and Pussycat Dolls alum Nicole Scherzinger and Laura Pausini, the Italian singer who helped open the Milan Cortina Olympics.

The trio performed the first ever official FIFA anthem, Desire, in coordinated outfits for the occasion.

Williams, who also performed the song at the World Cup draw in December, cut a particular striking figure.

The former Take That star raised eyebrows in a bedazzled electric blue tracksuit, the diamantes glimmering underneath the New Jersey sun.

Many viewers likened Williams to Paulie Walnuts, the fictional tracksuit mobster from The Sopranos series, on social media.

Oscar winner Jennifer Hudson was granted the honor of performing the US national anthem

The closing ceremony took place 90 minutes before kickoff between Spain and Argentina

Argentina fans arrive at MetLife Stadium before Sunday's hugely anticipated final vs Spain

Scherzinger wowed in a figure-hugging catsuit of the same color that featured a dramatic train, while Pausini looked ethereal in a flowing gown in a tie-dye print.

'Echoing the spirit of the opening ceremonies, which welcomed the world to the greatest stage in Canada, Mexico and the United States, the closing ceremony will bring the FIFA World Cup 2026 full circle through music, culture and football, before we kick off the highly anticipated match that will crown the champions of this groundbreaking tournament,' Heimo Schirgi, the World Cup's chief operating officer, had said of the event before the final.

This year's showstopper is bigger and better than ever with the star-studded event also boasting the first-ever World Cup halftime show, featuring the likes of Madonna, Shakira and Justin Bieber.

The ceremony took place following a morning of chaos in New York and New Jersey as thousands of fans descended on the Big Apple region for the final.

Those lucky enough to have clinched a ticket - or forked out as much as $10,000 for one - were urged to arrive up to four hours before the start of the game at the 80,000-seater stadium, a short drive outside of Manhattan.

FIFA encouraged fans to arrive early in order to participate in the World Cup closing ceremony, scheduled to begin around 90 minutes before the game itself kicks off.

But it has become standard procedure for fans to arrive even earlier for additional security checks whenever Trump attends a sporting event - lest they risk missing kickoff.

Trump has made it to plenty in his second term as President, ranging from the Ryder Cup to the Super Bowl, and his attendance often means lengthy delays for fans with airport-style security measures enforced for everyone making their way inside of the venue.

Fans had to pass heightened securoty measures due to President Trump's attendance

Thousands of fans and media members faced massive lines to enter the stadium for the World Cup final on Sunday amid several reports of security struggling to manage the situation

Delays on Sunday, however, were compounded amid reports of glitches in FIFA's ticket-scanning system, meaning those who were fortunate enough to be at the front of the long lines still faced frustrating delays.

Daily Mail also witnessed tensions simmering between fans, media members and security staff, with officials on the ground telling anyone who complained: 'Take it up with FIFA'.

But those members of security staff also appeared to be confused over how to manage the thousands of people arriving for the game.

There were multiple instances of organizers on the ground misdirecting people over where they should begin lining up to enter the stadium with over three hours to go until the start of the game.

Media members also faced extra checks from the secret service given the need to bring laptops and filming equipment inside of the stadium. DHS police and state police were also seen at the venue.

This all played out as other fans decided to leave it late to get to the stadium. With four hours to go until the game began, many supporters were still at Penn Station in Manhattan waiting to board a train into New Jersey and towards the stadium.

It is expected that Trump will be granted the honor of handing the trophy over to the victorious team.

The President carried out the same duties during the Club World Cup final, which also took place at MetLife Stadium.

He left the winning Chelsea stars, including Cole Palmer and Reece James, stunned when he remained on the stage throughout their celebrations.

Sports.title: Moronic Argentina fans run across TEN LANE highway in desperate bid to make World Cup final in time as travel hellscape bites
Sports.content:
Moronic Argentina fans run across TEN LANE highway in desperate bid to make World Cup final in time as travel hellscape bites

Desperate Argentina fans have been spotted running across a 10-lane New Jersey highway to make to the World Cup final as travel to MetLife Stadium became a hellscape.

A dozen fans were spotted trotting across busy lanes of traffic with MetLife in sight as some may have traveled from neighboring New York City, which became a nightmare to traverse after torrential rains flooded streets the night before.

Cars had to slow down and stop to allow the stragglers to safely cross.

Although traffic seemed fairly light outside of MetLife on Sunday, it is unclear what caused the fans to risked their lives to cross several lanes on the highway.

More than 80,000 fans are expected to descend on the New Jersey stadium to watch Argentina face Spain in the final at 3pm.

Much of the focus at the tournament has been on the weather, with France and England both seeing games delayed due to nature - be it extreme heat or lightning warnings.

And, for one final time, doubt has been cast over the kick-off time of the final this evening.

The streets of New York were flooded on the eve of the tournament's finale, with heavy rain causing mayhem. Cars were submerged and pedestrians were seen walking through chest-high water.

A dozen fans were spotted trotting across busy lanes of traffic on Sunday afternoon

More than 80,000 fans are expected to descend on the New Jersey stadium. Cars had to slow down and stop to allow the stragglers to safe cross

Between two and four inches of rain are said to have fallen, with a tornado warning also issued.

A flood watch covering eastern Bergen County, where MetLife is located, northeastern New Jersey and New York City remained in effect until 2am Sunday.

Although the heaviest rain had moved south and east by late Saturday afternoon, the National Weather Service warned that further storms could produce rainfall rates of one to two inches per hour.

The final showstopper between Spain and Argentina will be able to go ahead unaffected - but many fans may miss out.

While the worst of the horrific weather had passed by Sunday morning, leaving blue skies in its wake, the torrential conditions of the previous day left mayhem in its wake.

The dangerous conditions caused further turmoil at the region’s three major airports wrecking havoc for the thousands descending on New York and New Jersey.

Hundreds of flights into the New York area from across the United States were rocked by delays, or worse, cancellations as the downpours compounded travel problems.

Argentina fans are crossing the highway to get to MetLife pic.twitter.com/J2ATFbqA2q — Barstool Sports (@barstoolsports) July 19, 2026

Argentina plays Spain in the World Cup final at MetLife on Sunday

The stadium was within sight of the fans who raced to make the game

The Federal Aviation Administration ordered multiple ground stops at LaGuardia, JFK and Newark until at least 5pm ET on Saturday due to the thunderstorms.

Meanwhile, the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway was flooded, leaving drivers stranded on the washed-out roadway. Many sought safety on the roofs or bonnets of their vehicles as the water in some areas rose as high as car windows.

Sports.title: Ryan Fox WINS The Open in dramatic fashion as he birdies final hole at Royal Birkdale to triumph...39 years after his dad won the Rugby World Cup
Sports.content:
Chip off the old block, nerves of rock. Some 39 years after his father won the Rugby World Cup, Ryan Fox wrote another glorious chapter in a uniquely brilliant family story by winning The Open Championship on Sunday.

And how he did it, this Kiwi with the blood of an All Blacks legend. When push came to shove, on a day when four different men had hands on the Claret Jug, it was Ryan son of Grant who stepped forward and would not be beaten.

We should go straight to the moment of coronation before saying anything else. Because this 154th edition of golf’s oldest major went to the final putt of the final group on the final day.

By then, a little after 6.30pm on a breezy evening at these seaside links in Southport, Cameron Young had been killing time for more than two hours. For so long, his tally of nine under par appeared set to stand.

Even when Fox stood in the 18th fairway and flew an iron 172 yards through a crosswind to 11 feet, the smart money was on a play-off, because only five men out of 77 had birdied the last.

But the 78th man to try was Grant’s lad. And the thing about Grant is that he never missed – he was the fly-half with the metronomic boot and some traits don’t skip the generations. And so Fox pulled back that blade, brought it through, and after a small track from left to right the ball disappeared below ground.

Ryan Fox won The Open in dramatic fashion after he birdied the 18th hole on the final day

The New Zealander held his nerve under intense pressure to win his first ever major

Fox sank his putt on the 18th hole to trigger jubilant celebrations at Royal Birkdale in Southport

With two arms in the air, Fox was the Champion Golfer of Year.

‘Wow,’ he said in the immediate aftermath, having turned in a card for a 68 and a 10-under-par total. ‘I don't really know what to think at the moment.

‘I've got a lot of people to thank. First of all, my family, my wife and kids are in Florida at the moment. I spoke to my kids last night, and they said, “Bring back a trophy”. I think this is a pretty cool one to bring back for them.’

We can stick with the family theme a while longer, because it isn’t just Grant in the lineage – Fox’s maternal grandfather, Merv Wallace, also captained the New Zealand cricket team in the Fifties. With Fox the father to two daughters, one can only wonder what comes next.

But a word on the chasers in the here and now - Young was one behind after a 64, overnight leader Sam Burns was a spot further back with head of regrets, and they collectively stood ahead of a pair of challengers in Scottie Scheffler and a local lad named Tommy Fleetwood on seven under.

Had Fleetwood not bogeyed three in a row in the middle of his round, maybe this would have been his day. Maybe they would have closed the streets here for a year in celebration. But no one could begrudge a win for Fox, a 39-year-old who has walked the hard yards in this maddening game.

Fox became New Zealand’s second champion at The Open after Sir Bob Charles in 1963

The no-nonsense 39-year-old was speechless when reflecting on his triumph

After 14 years on the grind, he had already proven himself more than a familiar name with two PGA Tour wins and three on the European circuit, but he had never been higher than 23rd in the world. Arriving in Southport, he was ranked 56th and as recently as March underwent surgery to remove kidney stones. Men of a certain age can relate.

But then came this, which is to say an uplifting end to a thrilling day. Burns and Young can fight over who had the worst time of it, because Burns, runner up at the US Open last month, started two clear in his pairing with Fox and never turned up. All of the finesse and touch he used in building his lead vanished – he stepped on the fourth tee and went bogey-bogey-bogey and stayed at eight under for the rest of his day.

Young’s round was so very different. No one started better than this American nearly man, who started in 20th position and played the front nine in 29 strokes in the calmest conditions of the morning. For that matter, few did as well as him on the way in, either.

But standing on the 18th tee, at 10 under par, it went wrong. He drove into a pot bunker and then sought to attack the green from 180 yards short, only to thrash his shot into the face of the trap. Playing his third from the adjacent rough, Young’s third went into sand by the green and a bogey gave him an awful lot to think about on the two-hour wait for the later groups to finish.

Thankfully for Young, the wind was up. And when the wind is up on a baked links course, you have chaos and bogeys. Si Woo Kim avoided them for 10 holes and reached 10 under par, meaning he, Burns, Young and Fox all led at some point or other.

That he finished on six under told a story about the pressures of leading; that Bryson DeChambeau triple-bogeyed the 11th and capitulated to a 72 was possibly a different story about karma.

Had Scheffler birdied the 18th and reached nine under, who knows what kind of tremors that would have sent through the field. But instead he bogeyed and signed for a 67 and settled for seven under. Perhaps Fox wouldn’t have blinked anyway.

His round was steady in an even-par 34 for the front and a masterful clinic in rising at opportune moments on the back. Birdies at the 13th and 14th gave him his first taste of the lead and two more in the final three holes, when the pulse was thumping hardest, were the crowning moments of a champion.

Written in the stars, maybe, or more likely the DNA.

Sports.title: Bryson DeChambeau taunted with Rory McIlroy chants by fans at Royal Birkdale - as American suffers another meltdown at the Open following his controversial two-shot penalty
Sports.content:
In the end, those two shots made little difference after all. So much for the tantrums, the theatrics and the empty threats. Bryson DeChambeau, the man accused of holding the Open to ransom, was the one left to pay the price.

There was to be no final-day heroic march towards the Claret Jug, not even a finish close enough to eventual winner Ryan Fox for his army of fans to claim he’d been robbed.

Instead, it all died with DeChambeau losing his ball on the 11th and being driven back up the fairway to hit another with chants of ‘McIlroy, McIlroy, Rory McIlroy’ ringing in his ears.

Ever since the Northern Irishman stoked the fire on Saturday evening by accusing DeChambeau of ‘holding the tournament ransom’ after threatening to withdraw over his two-shot penalty for stomping down the long grass behind his ball, you always felt the Royal Birkdale crowd might not let him forget it.

The American had barely put his ball on the tee peg on the first hole when a bloke behind him piped up: ‘Rory’s going to buy you a pint after!’ to chortles and guffaws from the grandstand.

DeChambeau has done a fine job this week of making the 154th Open Championship all about him but a run of eight straight pars from the first felt all too straightforward. And then he stepped on to the 11th, having dropped a shot on the ninth, and it all unravelled.

He pulled his tee shot into the cabbage and could only cloth his second eight yards in front of him. He sent his third so deep into the thick stuff beside the green that he couldn’t find his ball and had to go back to hit another. The Birkdale crowd enjoyed that. DeChambeau took triple bogey and the chances of a third major were gone. A couple of birdies further down the stretch were in vain.

Bryson DeChambeau could not find a way to rally on the final day in his quest for the Claret Jug

The American was left enraged after receiving a two-shot penalty following his second round

A round of 72 saw him finish at four under. Having missed the cut in all three of the other majors this year, a finish of tied for 14th wasn’t too bad. Without the penalty, he’d have tied for sixth.

McIlroy had far from jumped to DeChambeau’s defence after the third round when asked if he thought he knew what he was doing when treading all over the grass around his ball on the fifth, which officials ruled was inadvertently improving his swing path. ‘I'm not in his mind -- but it didn't look good,’ he said.

DeChambeau received more support from world number one Scottie Scheffler yesterday. ‘He's a lot of things, but he's definitely not a cheater,’ said Scheffler. ‘I’ve never seen him cheat once, whether we were having a putting contest on the putting green or chipping contest.’

DeChambeau once again refused to do any post-round interviews but walked past a small group as he left and said: ‘Hope you guys have a great night, thank you’ before posing for a few selfies with fans - and a reporter - outside the media centre.

We’ll have to wait for his verdict on this most remarkable of weeks. You expect it might appear on his YouTube channel shortly.

Sports.title: Mayhem at World Cup final before Trump arrives as staff misdirect fans outside stadium and tension simmers over ticket issues - but Tom Cruise has no trouble getting in!
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

World Cup final day got off to a chaotic start at MetLife Stadium with fans forced to wait for hours outside of the venue amid reports of technological glitches scanning tickets and security staff unsure of how to manage the crowds.

Organizers this week urged fans lucky enough to have a ticket to arrive up to four hours before the start of the game at the 80,000-seater stadium in New Jersey, a short drive outside of Manhattan, for Sunday's showdown between Spain and Argentina.

As the build-up to the game expected to be watched by billions around the world ramped up, fans were waiting for over four hours to have their tickets scanned in order to enter the stadium for the showpiece game.

The attendance of President Donald Trump meant that airport-style security measures were also being enforced for everyone making their way inside of the venue.

But the delays were compounded amid reports of glitches in FIFA's ticket-scanning system, meaning those who were fortunate enough to be at the front of the long lines still faced frustrating delays.

The Daily Mail also witnessed tensions simmering between fans, media members and security staff, with officials on the ground telling anyone who complained: 'Take it up with FIFA'.

Thousands of fans and media members faced massive lines to enter the stadium for the World Cup final on Sunday amid several reports of security struggling to manage the situation

There were reports of tech issues and security misdirecting people around the stadium

Argentina fans arrive at MetLife Stadium before Sunday's hugely anticipated final vs Spain

But those members of security staff also appeared to be confused over how to manage the thousands of people arriving for the game.

There were multiple instances of organizers on the ground misdirecting people over where they should begin lining up to enter the stadium with over three hours to go until the start of the game.

Sky's Rob Harris also posted on X from the stadium: 'Fans told to get to the World Cup final stadium now 4 hours before KO - already security staff saying FIFA system glitches not scanning passes and long queues forming. With extra security. People being misdirected around the stadium with a lack of stewarding and staffing.'

Brazilian journalist Mariana Spinelli said it took her four hours to make it in, writing on X: 'We've been in line for 2 hours for the x-ray to ENTER the stadium. Everything disorganized, a total chaos. If this were in South America, they'd call us animals, third-world country. Since it's in the US nobody says anything. A nightmare of organization, pathetic.'

Media members also faced extra checks from the secret service given the need to bring laptops and filming equipment inside of the stadium. DHS police and state police were also seen at the venue.

This all played out as other fans decided to leave it late to get to the stadium. With four hours to go until the game began, many supporters were still at Penn Station in Manhattan waiting to board a train into New Jersey and towards the stadium.

The game is set to be the most expensive to attend in the history of sport - on Sunday morning, the cheapest ticket available on most resale websites was starting at around $7,000.

FIFA encouraged fans to arrive early in order to participate in the World Cup closing ceremony, scheduled to begin around 90 minutes before the game itself kicks off.

Extra security checks were in place ahead of the attendance of President Trump for the game

Tom Cruise had no such issue making his way inside before his closing ceremony appearance

But it is standard procedure for fans to arrive early for additional security checks whenever Trump attends a sporting event - and he has made it to plenty in his second term as President, ranging from the Ryder Cup to the Super Bowl.

Even on the live television coverage, the stadium was bare with a little over an hour until that closing ceremony began.

There weren't quite as many issues for the VIP guests, though. Tom Cruise was pictured sauntering into the venue - renamed as 'New York/New Jersey Stadium' for the tournament - ahead of his anticipated appearance in the closing ceremony.

Soccer greats such as Brazil World Cup winner Ronaldo, former England captain John Terry and former Argentina player Diego Simeone all appeared carefree as they entered the stadium in good time before the game.

Fans were slow to fill the stadium despite a call for them be in place for the closing ceremony

There were plenty of fans who were determined not to let the chaos ruin their day, too. Thousands of Argentina fans have made the journey to the stadium for what will likely be star man Lionel Messi's last ever appearance in a World Cup at the age of 39.

Argentina are narrow underdogs against Spain, the European champions, despite being the holders after winning the 2022 tournament in Qatar.

Trump is expected to hand the World Cup trophy over to the winning team after the game.

Sports.title: Terrified Zlatan Ibrahimovic swears live on TV during helicopter ride to World Cup final with Thierry Henry: 'If we go down, we go down together'
Sports.content:
He might be one of football's most braggadocious characters, but it turns out that Zlatan Ibrahimovic has a weak point after all: helicopter rides.

His fear of choppers is so great that he even admitted with a grin: 'I'm s*******in my pants!'

The Swedish giant, who stretches to 6ft5in and gave defenders nightmares throughout his career, looked petrified as he boarded a copter to the World Cup final.

Ibrahimovic, 44, has been working as a pundit for Fox Sports during the tournament alongside Thierry Henry and former United States star Alexi Lalas.

And after wiping some sweat off his brow, Ibrahimovic put on a brave face and tried to laugh off an impending flight to the final between Spain and Argentina in New Jersey.

He said: 'The adrenaline is pumping on the way, I'm s******* in my pants.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic admitted he was 's******* himself' ahead of a helicopter ride to the World Cup final

'I don't like helicopters but it's okay, I have Rebecca [Lowe, presenter] close to me, I have Thierry, I have Alexi.

'If we go down, we go down together.'

The former Manchester United, Barcelona, and Paris Saint-Germain striker was dressed to the nines in a cream suit for the air ride.

That was a departure from his attire on Saturday, when he went topless for a Cold as Balls interview show with Kevin Hart.

Zlatan doesn't tend to show vulnerability. He is known for his grandiose one-liners and self-exaltation, though it is often seen as an act.

He had this side to him even when he was a teenager. Offered a trial at Arsenal by Arsene Wenger, he recalls saying: 'I will not do a trial: either you take me or not, I'm not here to waste time.

'When I was young, in my mind no one was better than me.'

He has also said: 'I can't help but laugh at how perfect I am.'

Rebecca Lowe has spoken out on the tensions between Ibrahimovic and co-pundit Alexi Lalas

His personality has brought him into a jokey conflict with his co-pundit Lalas during the World Cup.

Recently, Fox World Cup host Lowe defiantly insisted that there is no tension between her colleagues Ibrahimovic and Lalas, despite multiple terse exchanges.

Ibrahimovic has branded Lalas 'the past' live on air and abruptly dismissed him for saying France were 'arrogant' in the first half against Senegal.

When Lalas then left the studio to report live from the Seattle stadium for the second United States group game, Ibrahimovic said: 'You're welcome, America.'

Footage also went viral from the Fox studio where the three analysts were playing soccer and Henry mercilessly tricked Lalas with a faked back heel while the cameras were rolling.

Host presenter Lowe, however, has insisted that the trio all get along fine when the cameras are off and claims that the suggestions of unrest behind the scenes is actually a source of amusement to all in the Fox setup.

Speaking to talkSPORT, Lowe said: 'These stories do make me laugh and we do laugh about them. We're like, "another one"? And it is getting a little out of hand.

'We are going through every newspaper now. Like, okay guys, maybe let's pivot and write about something else, that would be good. The football, maybe?'

Henry and Ibrahimovic posted a clip of themselves doing insane tricks, including one on Lalas

Lalas has attempted at times to get his own back, telling Ibrahimovic last weekend that his cream suit made him look like one of presenters on the 70s television show 'Fantasy Island'.

But Lowe says that amid the jokes the trio trade off at each other, there is an underlying respect between them all.

'There is nothing, there is no tension, nothing! We are laughing our heads off at all of this,' she added.

'Everybody respects everybody hugely. If people want to watch and listen to what the guys say to each other and work off each other, they would see that.

'It's a strange old narrative when you're in the middle of the thunderstorm, and I am right in the middle of it with them all day every day, and it just doesn't exist. It is crazy.'

Sports.title: Harry Kane insists England team-mates must stop talking about winning major silverware and focus on finally finishing the job after latest World Cup heartbreak
Sports.content:
Harry Kane insists England team-mates must stop talking about winning major silverware and focus on finally finishing the job after latest World Cup heartbreak

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Harry Kane has told his England team-mates that the talking about taking the final step on the road to silverware must stop and the time has come to just finish the job.

Thomas Tuchel’s squad still appeared in a state of shock as they left Miami following Saturday’s absurd 6-4 victory over France, which clinched third place at this World Cup.

The win secured a best-ever finish on foreign soil but the scars of their painful late semi-final defeat by Argentina are still evident.

Kane believes the manner of that defeat will linger for weeks and revealed that the group had been theorising over how best to deal with specific scenarios against the best opposition since losing the European Championship final to Spain in 2024.

‘The last 30 minutes of Argentina is not the team we want to be,’ Kane said. ‘We spent a lot of time over the last two years talking about that situation, to attack those moments. The bottom line is we lost anyway.

‘It’s easy to go away and talk about it. We need to get better at actually being in those situations.

Harry Kane has urged his England team-mates to prove they can go on and win a major tournament such as the World Cup

‘We have to learn, improve. The coach will have improved from these learnings. I can talk as much as I want but ultimately it’s about showing it next time we’re in that situation.’

Kane insisted that the Nations League campaign, which pits them against Spain, Croatia and Czechia from September, should better equipe England ahead of the home Euros.

And he has thrown his backing behind Tuchel amid fierce criticism from supporters and pundits for the way in which a one-goal lead against Argentina was managed.

‘It’s the enthusiasm he has, the emotion he brings, the tactical experience he has,’ Kane added. ‘It doesn’t mean you’re going to get it right every time. We want to get it right on the biggest occasions and he expects that from himself as well. He’s a fantastic coach.

‘It was his first major tournament. He’ll learn a lot from the players, the situations, the pressures, the travel. And the players will learn a lot from the other night.’

That the players had been discussing their inability to close out the biggest games before Tuchel’s arrival suggests that internally they will shoulder a portion of the blame.

Tuchel had appeared hurt by widespread condemnation, claiming that his first media conference since Argentina had felt as if England had been knocked out of the group stage without picking up a win.

England suffered a heart-breaking World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina

‘He not only gave the players belief but he gave the country belief that it was our year,’ the England captain said. ‘That is why it hurts even more than other years because everyone believed we were going all the way. Everyone has to process it. He has to process it himself.

‘We’re still in that grieving stage, the emotional stage, and we’ll be in that for the next few weeks.

‘It’s so hard. I think the fans are behind the team and are behind the manager. When something like this happens it’s very emotional – and rightly so. We’ve all been England fans when we wished we’d done this or that and it didn’t quite happen. That will die down naturally.

‘We had a lot of good things, a lot of tough situations we overcame. The group is incredible, the best England group I’ve been a part of in terms of togetherness. The boss was a big part of creating that as well.’

Sports.title: Donald Trump brutally booed at World Cup final as Spain and Argentina fans unite
Sports.content:
Donald Trump brutally booed at World Cup final as Spain and Argentina fans unite

Donald Trump was booed by fans at the 2026 World Cup final at MetLife Stadium just seconds after the national anthem

View 2 Images U.S. President Donald Trump was booed by fans inside the Met Life Stadium at the World Cup final (Image: (Photo by Eva Marie Uzcategui - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

Argentina and Spain fans made their feelings about Donald Trump crystal clear in booing the United States president when he appeared on the big screen at the World Cup Final. Trump had not attended the World Cup until the final, which caused a major headache for those attending the game.

‌



Federal agents, local law enforcement and private security firms had reportedly been mapping out Sunday's security operation for approximately two years, expecting the president to attend the tournament's showpiece event. However, technical problems meant scores of spectators and members of the media faced long delays getting into MetLife Stadium as measures were put in place following Trump's decision to attend.

‌



This, combined with his involvement with FIFA and Folarin Balogun's red card suspension being overturned, resulted in a mixed reception.

‌



Gary Lineker makes instant England prediction after France and responds to Bukayo Saka READ MORE :

Donald Trump picks his World Cup winner and makes request to Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Shortly before kick-off, just seconds after the national anthem concluded, Trump appeared on the giant screens inside MetLife Stadium.

The cheers that had accompanied the anthem quickly gave way to a chorus of boos, whistles, and jeers directed at the president, who had arrived via the Marine One helicopter and made a dramatic flyover of MetLife Stadium before the match got under way.

‌



Trump had been keen to avoid a repeat of his viral New York Knicks moment, while security teams left absolutely nothing to chance. F-16 fighter jets, military marksmen, and thousands of FBI agents were deployed to safeguard MetLife Stadium and the surrounding airspace.

The match has been designated a "Level 1" special event - the highest security classification in the US - putting it on a par with presidential inaugurations and State of the Union addresses.

View 2 Images United States President Donald Trump was booed (Image: Getty Images)

‌



A strictly enforced no-fly zone will cover the New York and New Jersey area from Friday through to Sunday's World Cup final, with snipers stationed on stadium rooftops and a heavily fortified perimeter set to cause considerable delays for supporters.

Once the final whistle blows and either Spain or Argentina are crowned champions, Trump is expected to hand over the iconic World Cup trophy to the victorious captain alongside FIFA president Gianni Infantino.

The 80-year-old was part of the celebrations when Chelsea lifted the trophy after beating Paris Saint-Germain in the Club World Cup Final last summer.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Trump and Infantino have cultivated a remarkably close bond - unlike anything previously witnessed between a FIFA president and a world leader - which culminated in the extraordinary inaugural awarding of the FIFA Peace Prize last December at the World Cup draw.

Ahead of the World Cup Final, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt defended the sheer scale of the security operation, framing Trump's attendance as the crowning moment of the entire tournament.

Article continues below

"His attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure and most successful World Cup in American history," Leavitt said.

Sports.title: Scottie Scheffler breaks silence on Bryson DeChambeau penalty controversy at The Open
Sports.content:
Scottie Scheffler breaks silence on Bryson DeChambeau penalty controversy at The Open

Bryson DeChambeau was handed a two-shot penalty during The Open after he was deemed to have improved his lie during his second round, with world number one Scottie Scheffler now weighing in on the matter

View 2 Images Scottie Scheffler has broken his silence on the Bryson DeChambeau controversy (Image: Sky Sports)

Controversial golf star Bryson DeChambeau is 'definitely not a cheater', according to world number one Scottie Scheffler, after the bolshy American received a two-shot penalty at The Open following an inadvertent breach when he improved his lie during his second round.

‌



Scheffler believes more players are pushing the lines on what is permitted on the course and he has suggested that the type of incidents which landed DeChambeau in hot water require stricter oversight, with the penalised superstar facing greater scrutiny than most. However, he believes that DeChambeau was sloppy rather than deliberately dishonest in his actions.

‌



The four-time major champion had previously stayed tight-lipped on the subject, stating: "I do have a ton to say. I haven't decided exactly what I want to say publicly yet."

‌



But now he's broken his silence on the controversy. "I think that opens up a greater discussion that - all I can really say is I think maybe we need to be a little bit more strict in the way that we are policing guys," Scheffler remarked.

"But it's a little bit of a balance because you've got certain guys like a Bryson who every shot he hits is going to be shown on TV. When you have camera angles that are far away, things can look different than they do when you're right there.

Scottie Scheffler rages at The Open as tempers flare in dramatic scenes READ MORE :

"We've done a good job of - I don't know, I hate saying stuff out here because I don't want anything to get taken out of context. All I'll say is Bryson, I've known him for a long time, and he's a lot of things, but he's definitely not a cheater.

‌



"I've never seen him cheat once, whether we were having a putting contest on the putting green or chipping contest, or anytime we played amateur golf, I never saw anything suspicious.

"When you're watching him there from that camera angle, maybe he was a touch careless around his ball, but I don't think he did anything intentionally.

View 2 Images Bryson DeChambeau was angered by his penalty following the second round of The Open (Image: Getty)

‌



"We've seen penalties happen with - like you remember Jon Rahm a couple years ago at the Memorial when his ball moved in the rough, and it's like to the naked eye, can you really tell that?".

"I think sometimes it's just a difficult position in the game of golf. When I was growing up, if this was the line between things that were - like if this was the line, here are the rules and this was the right side of it and this is when you're doing things against the rule, you always tried to stray really far that way. I feel like at times, sometimes you see players maybe push it a little bit further than they should."

Two-time US Open champion DeChambeau became embroiled in a prolonged and heated exchange with R&A rules officials before the penalty was handed down. That post-round confrontation resulted in a delay to the release of Saturday's tee times.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Rory McIlroy made clear he felt it was beside the point whether DeChambeau had cheated or not, expressing his frustration at the American's conduct. The Ryder Cup stalwart accused DeChambeau of holding the tournament to ransom and was scathing in his assessment.

"I think there's no doubt that he improved the line of his backswing," McIlroy said. "Whether it was careless or whether it was intentional, I don't think it matters. Hopefully it was careless, but I think the two-shot penalty was justified for sure.

Article continues below

"I won't pretend to defend Bryson," he continued. "I'm not particularly fond of him. I think a lot of it's performative. I think a lot of it's for attention.

"To hold the tournament hostage like that, and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn't feel like it was a great look."

Sports.title: Harry Kane tells England teammates where they must improve before Euro 2028
Sports.content:
Harry Kane tells England teammates where they must improve before Euro 2028

England secured their best finish at a World Cup since 1966 by beating France in the bronze playoff on Saturday evening and Three Lions' captain Kane has issued a message to his teammates

View 4 Images Kane has helped England to third place at the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

Harry Kane insists England should be “proud” of their World Cup - even if it will take time to get over the disappointment.

‌



England produced one of the all-time great World Cup matches in their ten goal thriller with France which also delivered their best performance in the tournament on foreign soil.

‌



Thomas Tuchel’s men left the United States with a bronze medal even if Kane says the whole squad is still wracked with regret and disappointment.

‌



England captain Kane said: “A lot of positives. Obviously people are going to be talking about it already. It’s the highest finish in 60 years, the highest finish on foreign soil. There is a lot to be proud of.

“Of course we’re still feeling it from the other night, the emotion and the what ifs. That will be with us for a while now.

“I’m proud of the boys, how we approached this game. It wasn’t easy to find the mentality. We said before that every time you represent England it should be a proud moment. It’s the least we deserved, to grab a medal.

‌



Spain star calls out Donald Trump and confirms if he'll shake his hand at World Cup final READ MORE :

Argentina stars taunted England from team bus after World Cup win as cutting message revealed READ MORE :

“The game is impossible to judge because it’s a complete opposite to what that would’ve been if it was a final. It shows the quality we have. To score six against anyone you have to play a certain way and play well.

“Every time you get closer, knock on the door. You think you’ve learned and you have but we just have to keep going.”

Bukayo Saka scored a hat-trick, Declan Rice was on target and provided an assist for Ezri Konsa while Jude Bellingham got a brilliant sixth to finally put the game to bed.

‌



France mounted an astonishing comeback from 4-0 down at half time as Kylian Mbappe scored twice, Bradley Barcola was on target while Ousmane Dembele also scored.

View 4 Images Harry Kane is still determined to lead England to silverware (Image: Getty Images)

It felt at 4-3 that it was going to come crumbling down for England and that collapse would have opened up old wounds from the semi-final defeat to Argentina.

‌



But what it did do was change the mood. There were boos before the game when England boss Tuchel’s name was read out. The fans are hurting and angry.

Football does move quickly and the heroics in Mexico City followed by the win against Norway are forgotten amid the collapse against Argentina.

But, equally, this should be a game-changer in the other direction. Tuchel needed a quick reaction and it felt like his players, despite the heartbreak, wanted to send a message.

‌



View 4 Images Harry Kane speaks with Thomas Tuchel (Image: Getty Images)

Even if that message was partly what might have been. Saka hit a hat trick and was brilliant which quickly leaves everyone cursing Tuchel for not playing him more.

But that is unfair because Saka has not been at his best. Rice was also brilliant as he wore the armband but he has also struggled because of fitness issues.

‌



Rather than look back with recriminations, England need to embrace the first half performance and enjoy the positives and energy. Eberechi Eze driving forward from midfield. Djed Spence having another blinder. Marc Guehi and Konsa defending well.

This was France and, despite the fightback and crazy nature of the game, England lost in their last two third-place games in 1990 and 2018 and so this was something to be proud of no matter the fact they wished the game had been the final.

View 4 Images England's third place finish is their best at a World Cup since 1966 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Kane was given a rare day off but talked as captain on behalf of the group and now believes they must use the failings as “motivation” but also learn from their mistakes and take them into the Nations League campaign and Euro 2028.

Kane added: “It’s easy to go away and talk about it. We need to get better at actually being in those situations. We can train, play the qualifiers… I think the Nations League will be big for us, against Spain and Croatia, big teams.

“Getting used to those big environments and finding our best form against those teams, like we did against France – albeit not in the most competitive match. We have to learn, improve.

‌



“The coach will have improved from these learnings. I can talk as much as I want but ultimately it’s about showing it next time we’re in that situation.

“We still showed signs of what we showed the other night unfortunately, when they started to come back into the game. We couldn’t quite get the pressure on the ball and keep the ball. There is stuff we need to improve on.

“We know over the next two years until we’re facing that situation again there is always going to be a question mark. It’s something we have to take and use as motivation.”

Sports.title: Lewis Hamilton punishment confirmed after Belgian GP incident left F1 star with broken leg fear
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton punishment confirmed after Belgian GP incident left F1 star with broken leg fear

A frightening pit lane incident at the Belgian Grand Prix saw Lewis Hamilton accidentally drive into a member of Ferrari's crew, sparking worries of serious damage

View 2 Images Lewis Hamilton hit a mechanic (Image: X)

Ferrari have been fined £25,512 after Lewis Hamilton accidentally hit a crew member with his car during a terrifying pit lane accident at the Belgian Grand Prix. Hamilton was shown the green light during a pit stop, signalling that it was safe for him to pull away and get back onto the track at Spa-Francorchamps.

‌



However, the seven-time Formula 1 champion immediately checked in on the mechanic, who was attempting to adjust his front wing very late on, via his team radio. While the member of staff fortunately didn't sustain any serious damage, Hamilton has since admitted that his heart sank as he quickly remembered how Kimi Raikkonen had broke a mechanic's leg in Bahrain in a similar incident.

‌



Speaking after the Belgian GP, Hamilton said: "The green light went, and so I went. You're looking over here [at the light] and not over there [at the mechanic].

‌



Lewis Hamilton punished at Belgian GP after taking out George Russell in first-lap crash READ MORE :

"That's more on the team, ultimately. But when it happened, I noticed him and I stopped and what went through my mind at that moment was when Kimi hit and broke the leg, and my heart really sank for a second."

While the mechanic thankfully was not hurt in the process, Ferrari were unable to escape punishment for the incident, with the FIA announcing a sizeable fine to go Scuderia's way.

A notice read: "The competitor (Scuderia Ferrari HP) is fined €30,000 of which €10,000 is suspended for 12 months on condition that the Competitor does not commit a similar infringement in the meantime and on the further condition that within 14 days the Competitor submits a report to the FIA regarding the incident and protocols introduced to mitigate the risk of such an incident occurring in the future."

‌



It added: "The Stewards heard from the team representative and reviewed video evidence. As Car 44 was being released from its pit stop, a mechanic stepped in the path of the front right tyre as the F1 Car moved forward. He fell but was not injured.

"The team explained the incident occurred in the context of a complex and unusual combination of circumstances. HAM had been issued a 5 second time penalty for a driving infringement which had to be served before work could commence on the F1 Car.

‌



"LEC was in his pit box at the point HAM entered the pit lane. HAM told his engineer that he wanted a front wing adjustment but that was not conveyed to the super controller.

"HAM came into his pit box, served the time penalty and at the end of the 5 seconds one member of the team announced 'Go' and then '0.6 degrees,' the former being an instruction to commence the pit stop and the latter being an instruction for a wing adjustment.

"The tyre change was completed, the jack-man dropped the F1 Car and the super controller activated the green light signal for Car 44 to move off. Just as the driver moved off, another mechanic with a front wing tool moved forward into the path of the front right tyre. Before he stepped forward he had his head down looking at the tool and did not see the green light.

‌



View 2 Images Lewis Hamilton finished fourth in Belgium (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

"The team acknowledged that for Car 44 to have been released in these circumstances was unsafe and attributed the error to an inappropriately late instruction for the wing adjustment, a lack of clear communication and the mechanic’s failure to notice the green light.

"The team committed to undertaking a review of their pit stop procedures to ensure an incident such as this will not be repeated. The Stewards determined that the driver was in no respect at fault."

Hamilton claimed a fourth-place finish in Belgium, with Kimi Antonelli winning the race while Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen joined him on the podium. As a result, Hamilton sits second in the Drivers' Championship standings, 45 points behind Antonelli.
